the exhaustion of the fetters to be abandoned through the truths of suffering and origin within the form and formless realms constitutes the second knowledge of abandonment.
The exhaustion of the fetters to be abandoned by the truth of cessation in the desire realm constitutes the third knowledge of abandonment;
the exhaustion of the fetters to be abandoned by the truth of cessation in the form and formless realms constitutes the fourth knowledge of abandonment;
and the exhaustion of the fetters to be abandoned by the truth of the path in the desire realm constitutes the fifth knowledge of abandonment.
The exhaustion of the fetters to be abandoned by the Path-truth in the realms of form and formlessness constitutes six knowledges of abandonment;
the exhaustion of the five lower fetters constitutes seven knowledges of abandonment;
and the exhaustion of craving for the realm of form constitutes eight knowledges of abandonment.
When all fetters are exhausted, there are nine knowledges of abandonment (*prahāṇajñāna*).
Do the nine knowledges of abandonment encompass all knowledges of abandonment, or do all knowledges of abandonment encompass the nine knowledges of abandonment?
There are eight types of persons:

Those who are entering the stream and have realized the fruit of stream-entry; those who are entering once-returning and have realized the fruit of once-returning; those who are entering non-returning and have realized the fruit of non-returning; and those who are entering arhatship and have realized the fruit of arhatship.
Regarding one who is practicing for the realization of *srotāpanna*, how many of the nine knowledges of abandonment (*prahāṇajñāna*) have they accomplished, and how many have they not accomplished?

This continues up to one who is practicing for the realization of *arhat* and has realized *arhatship*: regarding the nine knowledges of abandonment, how many have they accomplished, and how many have they not accomplished?
I wish to explain in full the meaning of this chapter.
There are nine fetters (*saṃyojana*):

the fetter of craving, the fetter of ill-will, the fetter of conceit, the fetter of ignorance, the fetter of views, the fetter of adherence to precepts and observances, the fetter of doubt, the fetter of stinginess, and the fetter of envy.
If within one's body there is the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: It is so;
if there is the fetter of ill-will, then there is the fetter of craving.
Is there a case where the fetter of attachment exists but the fetter of aversion does not?
Answer: Yes;
for example, when the fetter of attachment to phenomena of the form and formless realms has not yet been exhausted.
If within the body there is the fetter of craving, is there also conceit?
The answer is: Yes.
If there is conceit, is there also the fetter of craving?
Answer: It is so.
If there is the fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana) binding within the body, is there also the fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana)?
Answer: It is so;
where there is the fetter of craving, there is also the fetter of ignorance.
Is there ignorance without the fetter of craving?
The answer is: Yes.

When the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of origination has not yet arisen, and if among the phenomena to be abandoned by the truth of suffering, the fetter of ignorance to be abandoned by the truth of origination has not been exhausted:
if there is the bond of the fetter of craving within this body, is there also the bond of the fetter of views?
Answer: There may be craving, yet no views.
How is it that there is craving but no views?
Answer:

When the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen; if the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇāsaṃyojana*) associated with the views to be abandoned by the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*) and the truth of the path (*mārgasatya*) has not been exhausted; or if the fetter of craving associated with the factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāheya*) has not been exhausted.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, if the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) associated with the views to be abandoned by the truth of the path has not been exhausted, or if the fetter of craving associated with the factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) has not been exhausted.
When a disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths has not yet exhausted the fetter of craving for those dharmas to be abandoned through cultivation, this is called "craving but not view.
What is "view but not craving"?
Answer:

When the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of the origin has not yet arisen, and the fetters of views to be abandoned by the truth of suffering and the fetters to be abandoned by the truth of the origin have not been exhausted—this is called "view, but not craving."
What is meant by being bound by both?
The answer is:
when all the limbs and joints of a person’s body are bound, or when one is bound by both [the fetters] regarding the dharmas to be abandoned through the contemplation of the Four Truths.

When the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of the origin has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] regarding those phenomena abandoned through the cultivation of the truth of the origin and the truth of the path.

When the knowledge of the origin has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] regarding those phenomena associated with the views to be abandoned through the truth of cessation and the truth of the path.

When the knowledge of exhaustion has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [types of fetters] regarding the factors associated with the views to be abandoned through the truth of the path.
This is called being bound by both within the person.
What is meant by "neither being bound to both within the body"?
The answer is:

when the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*kṣaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is not bound to either of the two categories of phenomena abandoned through the truth of suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) or the truth of origination (*samudaya-satya*).

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is unbound from both [categories] regarding those phenomena to be abandoned by the truths of suffering, origin, and cessation.
For a disciple of the Blessed One who has attained vision of the truths, one is unbound from both [categories] regarding those phenomena to be abandoned by the four truths.
When craving for the realm of desire has been exhausted, one is unbound from both types of phenomena in the realm of desire.
When craving for the realms of form and formlessness has been exhausted, one is unbound from both types of phenomena in the realms of form and formlessness.
This is called the body being unbound by both.
The same applies to doubt.
If the body is bound by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is it also bound by the fetter of wrong resolve (*parāmarśa-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:
There may be craving, yet no failure of resolve.
What is meant by having craving but no failure of resolve?

Answer: When the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of craving for phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāheya-dharmatṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) is not yet exhausted.
When the knowledge of exhaustion has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of craving for phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation is not yet exhausted.

When a disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths still has not exhausted the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) regarding those phenomena to be abandoned by reflection, this is called having craving but no wish for loss (*apraṇidhāna*).
What is meant by having a wish for loss but no craving?
Answer:

When the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of the origin has not yet arisen, if the fetter of the loss of resolve (*parāmarśa*)—which is to be abandoned through the truth of suffering and the truth of the origin—is not yet exhausted, this is called the loss of resolve without craving.
What is meant by "the body being bound by both"? Answer:
When all the limbs and joints of a person's body are bound, they are bound by both [types of fetters] regarding those dharmas to be abandoned through the contemplation of the Four Truths.

When the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of the origin has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] regarding those phenomena abandoned through the cultivation of the truth of the origin and the truth of the path.

When the knowledge of the origin has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] regarding those phenomena abandoned through the cultivation of the truth of cessation and the truth of the path.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] regarding those phenomena to be abandoned by the truth of the path.
This is called being bound by both.
What is meant by being unbound by both?
Answer:

When the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*kṣaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is unbound from both categories of dharmas abandoned through the truth of suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) and the truth of origination.

When the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārga-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is unbound from both categories of dharmas abandoned through the truths of suffering, origination, and cessation.
A disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths is unbound from both [types of fetters] regarding those dharmas abandoned by the four truths.
When desire for the realm of desire is exhausted, one is unbound from both [types of fetters] regarding the dharmas of the desire realm.
When craving for the form and formless realms is exhausted, one is unbound by both types of phenomena pertaining to the form and formless realms.
This is called being unbound by both in relation to the body.
If the fetter of craving binds the body, is there also the fetter of stinginess?
He replied: "It is so;
where there is stinginess, there is craving.
Is it possible, however, for there to be craving without stinginess?"
Answer:

There are those who have not yet exhausted the fetter of craving for the dharmas to be abandoned through the vision of the Four Truths within the desire realm, and so on, up to those who have not yet exhausted the fetter of craving for the dharmas of the form and formless realms.
Envy is also like this. This concludes the section on the gate of craving.
The gateway of conceit is also like this.
If within one’s body there is the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*), is there also the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)? Answer:
In this way, if there is the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*), is there also the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Could there be conceit without ill-will?
He replied:
Regarding the dharmas of the form and formless realms, the fetter of conceit (*māna*) has not yet been exhausted.
If within one's person there is the binding of the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda*), is there also the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā*)?
Answer: Yes.
In this way, where there is hatred, there is ignorance.
Is it possible for there to be ignorance without hatred?
He replied:

There is one for whom sensual craving has not yet been exhausted; who has already produced the knowledge of suffering but not yet produced the knowledge of its origin; and for whom the fetter of ignorance to be abandoned by the truth of suffering and the fetter of ignorance to be abandoned by the truth of its origin within the desire realm have not yet been exhausted, as well as the fetter of ignorance regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms that has not yet been exhausted.
If there is the fetter of ill-will (pratigha-saṃyojana) binding within the body, is there also the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana)?
Answer: There may be ill-will without views.
What is the state of having hatred but no [wrong] views?
The answer is:

when craving for the realm of desire (*kāmarāga*) has not yet been exhausted; when the knowledge of the origin (*samudayajñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen; and when, within the realm of desire, the fetter of hatred (*pratighasaṃyojana*) associated with factors to be abandoned by the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*) and the truth of the path (*mārgasatya*) has not yet been exhausted, as well as the fetter of hatred associated with factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāheya*) within the realm of desire has not yet been exhausted.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (kṣayajñāna) has arisen but the knowledge of the path (mārgajñāna) has not yet arisen, the fetter of ill-will (vyāpādasaṃyojana) associated with views that are to be abandoned by the truth of the path within the desire realm is not yet exhausted; likewise, the fetter of ill-will regarding phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation within the desire realm is not yet exhausted.

When a disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths has not yet exhausted sensual desire, and has not yet exhausted the fetter of ill-will regarding the dharmas of the desire realm to be abandoned through cultivation, this is called having ill-will but no views.
What is meant by "viewing without hatred"?
The answer is:

when desire-love is not yet exhausted, the knowledge of suffering has already arisen but the knowledge of origination has not yet arisen; within the desire realm, the fetters of views to be abandoned through the truth of suffering and the truth of origination are not yet exhausted, and the fetters of views regarding the dharmas of the form and formless realms are not yet exhausted—this is called viewing without hatred.
What is meant by "the body being bound by both"?
The answer is:

when the limbs and joints of a person's body are entirely bound, they are bound by both [types of fetters] regarding the dharmas to be abandoned through the contemplation of the Four Truths within the realm of desire.

When craving for the desire realm has not yet been exhausted, and the knowledge of suffering has already arisen while the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] to the phenomena of the desire realm that are abandoned through cultivation regarding the truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

When the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] regarding the factors associated with views that are to be abandoned through the truth of cessation and the truth of the path within the desire realm.

When the knowledge of exhaustion has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is bound by both regarding the factors associated with views that are to be abandoned through the truth of the path within the desire realm.
This is called the body being bound by both.
What is the body being unbound by both? Answer:

When the knowledge of origination has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion has not yet arisen, one is unbound from both categories of phenomena abandoned through the vision of the truth of suffering and the truth of origination; one is also unbound from the categories of phenomena abandoned through cultivation in the realms of form and formlessness.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is bound by neither [of these two knowledges] regarding those dharmas to be abandoned through the truths of suffering, origin, and cessation; likewise, one is bound by neither regarding those dharmas of the form and formless realms to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
A disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths is unbound from both [types of fetters] regarding those dharmas abandoned by the four truths.
When sensual craving is exhausted, one is unbound from both [types of fetters] regarding the dharmas of the desire realm.
When craving for the form and formless realms is exhausted, one is unbound from both types of phenomena pertaining to the form and formless realms.
This is called being unbound from both in relation to the body.
The same applies to doubt.
If within one's body there is the fetter of ill-will, is there also the loss of resolve?
Answer: There may be ill-will without the loss of resolve.
What is meant by having hatred but not having the loss of resolve?
The answer is:

when desire-attachment is not yet exhausted, the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, and hatred toward the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned through mental cultivation (*bhāvanāprahātavya*) is not yet exhausted.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the hatred to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) regarding the desire realm has not been exhausted.

For a disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths (*satyābhisamaya*), if sensual craving (*kāmarāga*) is not yet exhausted, the hatred to be abandoned through cultivation regarding the desire realm has not been exhausted.
This is called being free from ill will while not being free from the failure of one's vows.
What is meant by being free from the failure of one's vows while not being free from ill will?
The answer is:

When sensual craving has not yet been exhausted, and the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen while the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; when the loss of resolve regarding the factors to be abandoned by the truth of suffering and the truth of origination within the desire realm has not yet been exhausted, and the loss of resolve regarding the factors of the form and formless realms has not yet been exhausted—this is called "loss of resolve without ill will."
What is meant by being bound by both?
The answer is:

when the body and all its limbs and joints of a person are completely bound, they are bound by both [the fetters] regarding the dharmas of the desire realm that are to be abandoned through the contemplation of the four truths.

When craving for the desire realm has not yet been exhausted, and the knowledge of suffering has already arisen but the knowledge of the origin has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] regarding those phenomena of the desire realm that are to be abandoned through the cultivation of the truth of the origin and the truth of the path.

When the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] regarding those factors in the desire realm to be abandoned by the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*) and the truth of the path (*mārgasatya*).

When the knowledge of exhaustion has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [fetters] regarding those factors in the desire realm to be abandoned by the truth of the path.
This is called the body being bound by both.
What is the body being liberated from both?
The answer is:

When the knowledge of the origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is liberated from both categories of phenomena to be abandoned through the vision of the truth of suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) and the truth of the origin; one is also liberated from both categories of phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) belonging to the realms of form and formlessness.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is liberated from both categories of phenomena to be abandoned by the truths of suffering, origin, and cessation; one is also liberated from both categories of phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanāheya*) within the realms of form and formlessness.

A disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths is liberated from both types of factors abandoned through the vision of the four truths; they are also liberated from both types of factors abandoned through cultivation in the realms of form and formlessness.
When sensual craving has been exhausted, one is liberated from both [the fetters] regarding the phenomena of the desire realm.
When craving for the form and formless realms has been exhausted, one is liberated from both [the fetters] regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms.
This is called bodily liberation from both.
If within the body there is the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*), is there also the fetter of stinginess (*mātsarya-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: It is so;
where there is the fetter of stinginess, there is the fetter of ill-will.
Is there a case where the fetter of ill-will exists but the fetter of avarice does not?
Answer: Yes;
for example, when the ill-will directed toward phenomena in the desire realm to be abandoned by the vision of the Four Truths has not yet been exhausted.
The fetter of envy is also like this; [this concludes the section on] ill will.
If there is the binding of the fetter of ignorance within one's person, is there also the fetter of views?
Answer: Yes.
Thus, where there is seeing, there is ignorance (*avidyā*).
Is it possible for there to be ignorance without seeing?
He replied:

When the knowledge of cultivation has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion has not yet arisen, the fetter of ignorance associated with views—which are to be abandoned by the truth of cessation and the truth of the path—is not yet exhausted; likewise, the fetter of ignorance regarding phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation is not yet exhausted.

When the knowledge of exhaustion has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, the fetter of ignorance associated with the views to be abandoned by the truth of the path is not yet exhausted, and the fetter of ignorance regarding the factors to be abandoned by cultivation is not yet exhausted.
For a disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths (*dṛṣṭiprāpta*), the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) is not yet exhausted.
The same applies to doubt (*vicikitsā*).
If there is the binding of the fetter of ignorance within one's person, is there also the fetter of wrong resolve (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: It is so;
where there is wrong resolve (mithyāpraṇidhāna), there is ignorance (avidyā).
Is it possible for there to be ignorance without wrong resolve?
Answer: There is.

When the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of ignorance (*avidyāsaṃyojana*) regarding phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāheya*) is not yet exhausted.

When the knowledge of exhaustion has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of ignorance regarding phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation is not yet exhausted.
For a disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths, the fetter of ignorance regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) is not yet exhausted.
If there is the bondage of the fetter of ignorance within that person's continuum, is there also the fetter of stinginess (*mātsarya*)?
Answer: It is so;
where there is the fetter of stinginess (*mātsarya-saṃyojana*), there is ignorance (*avidyā*).
Is it possible, however, for there to be ignorance without stinginess?
Answer: Yes.

There are those for whom the fetter of ignorance regarding the dharmas to be abandoned by the four truths of the desire realm has not been exhausted, and those for whom the fetter of ignorance regarding the dharmas of the form and formless realms has not been exhausted.
Envy is also like this. [The section on the gate of delusion concludes.]
If within a person there is the fetter of views (dṛṣṭisaṃyojana), is there also the loss of resolve (icchantikatā)?
The answer is: It is so;
where there is the fetter of views, there is also the loss of resolve.
Is there a case where the fetter of wrong resolve (*īrṣyā*) is present but the view [of self] is not?
Answer: Yes.

When the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of wrong resolve regarding those factors dissociated from the views to be abandoned by the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*) and the truth of the path (*mārgasatya*) has not yet been exhausted.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the factors dissociated from the views to be abandoned by the truth of the path (*mārgasatya*), as well as the loss of aspiration (*praṇidhānavipanna*), have not yet been exhausted.
If, within this body, there is the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*), is there also the fetter of doubt (*vicikitsāsaṃyojana*)?
Answer: There are those who possess views but have no doubt.
How is it that one possesses views yet has no doubt?
Answer:

When the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*) associated with the views to be abandoned by the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*) and the truth of the path (*mārgasatya*) has not yet been exhausted.

When the knowledge of exhaustion has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of views associated with the views to be abandoned by the truth of the path has not yet been exhausted.
This is called having vision but no doubt.
What is meant by having doubt but no vision?
The answer is:

When the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of doubt (*vicikitsā-saṃyojana*) associated with the states abandoned by the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*) and the truth of the path (*mārgasatya*) has not been fully eliminated.

When the knowledge of exhaustion has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of doubt associated with the states abandoned by the truth of the path has not been fully eliminated.
This is called the absence of views regarding doubt.
What is meant by "the body being bound by both"?
The answer is:
When the limbs and joints of the human body are all bound, one is bound by both [types of fetters] regarding those phenomena abandoned through the contemplation of the Four Truths.

When the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [types of fetters] regarding those phenomena abandoned through the contemplation of the truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
This is called the body being bound by both.
What is the body being liberated from both? Answer:

When the knowledge of the origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is liberated from both regarding the factors abandoned by the truth of suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) and the truth of the origin; one is liberated from both regarding the factors associated with views and doubt that are abandoned by the truth of exhaustion and the truth of the path (*mārga-satya*); and one is liberated from both regarding the factors abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of exhaustion has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, there is liberation from both [types of fetters] regarding the phenomena to be abandoned by the truth of suffering, the truth of origination, and the truth of cessation; there is liberation from both regarding the phenomena associated with views and doubt that are to be abandoned by the truth of the path; and there is liberation from both regarding the phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation.
A disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths is liberated from both types of factors abandoned by the four truths.
When craving for the desire realm is exhausted, they are liberated from both types of factors of the desire realm.
When craving for the form and formless realms is exhausted, one is liberated from both types of phenomena pertaining to the form and formless realms.
This is called bodily liberation from both.
If within a person's continuum there is the fetter of views, is there also the fetter of stinginess?
Answer: There are cases where there is wrong view but no stinginess.
What is meant by having wrong view but no stinginess?
Answer:

When the fetter of views regarding the phenomena to be abandoned through the vision of the Four Truths in the desire realm has not been exhausted, and the fetter of views regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms has not been exhausted, this is called "view-attachment" (dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa).
What is stinginess that is not view?
The answer is:

when desire-attachment is not yet exhausted, the knowledge of cultivation has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion has not yet arisen, and the fetter of stinginess regarding phenomena to be abandoned through the contemplation of the desire realm is not yet exhausted.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of stinginess (*mātsaryasaṃyojana*) regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāprahātavya*) is not yet exhausted.

For a disciple of the Blessed One who has attained the vision of the truths (*satyadarśana*), if sensual craving (*kāmarāga*) is not yet exhausted, the fetter of stinginess regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation is not yet exhausted.
This is called stinginess that is not [associated with] views.
What is meant by "the body being bound by both"? Answer:
When all the limbs and joints of the human body are bound, one is bound by both [types of fetters] regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm.

When desire for the desire realm is not yet exhausted, and the knowledge of suffering has already arisen but the knowledge of origination has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [types of fetters] regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm.
This is called being bound by both.
What is meant by being liberated from both?
The answer is:

When the knowledge of the origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*kṣaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is liberated from both [types of] factors to be abandoned by the truths of suffering and its origin; one is liberated from both types of factors associated with views that are not dissociated [from the mind] and to be abandoned by the truths of cessation and the path; and one is liberated from both types of factors of the form and formless realms to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, there is twofold liberation from those dharmas to be abandoned by the truths of suffering, its origin, and cessation; twofold liberation from those dharmas associated with views that are to be abandoned by the truth of the path; and twofold liberation from those dharmas of the form and formless realms to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

For a disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths, there is liberation from both types of dharmas abandoned through the vision of the four truths; likewise, there is liberation from both types of dharmas abandoned through cultivation in the realms of form and formlessness.
When craving for the realm of desire has been exhausted, one is liberated from both types of phenomena pertaining to the realm of desire.
When craving for the realms of form and formlessness has been exhausted, one is liberated from both types of phenomena pertaining to the realms of form and formlessness.
This is called liberation from both.
Envy is also like this; the fifth section on views is concluded, having passed through four [sections].
If there is the fetter of the vow-breaking (pradāśa) binding within one's body, is there also the fetter of doubt (vicikitsā)?
Answer: Yes.
In this way, where there is the fetter of doubt, there is the loss of resolve.
Is it possible to have the loss of resolve without doubt?
The answer is: Yes.

There is [the case where] the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has already arisen, but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen; the fetter of wrong resolve (*parāmarśasaṃyojana*) has not been exhausted regarding those factors dissociated from doubt that are to be abandoned by the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*) and the truth of the path (*mārgasatya*).

Or, the knowledge of exhaustion has already arisen, but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen; the fetter of wrong resolve has not been exhausted regarding those factors dissociated from doubt that are to be abandoned by the truth of the path.
If within a person's continuum there is the fetter of the vow-violation (pradāśa-saṃyojana), is there also the fetter of stinginess (mātsarya-saṃyojana)?
Answer: There may be the vow-violation fetter without the stinginess fetter.
What is meant by having the fetter of wishing-for-loss (icchā-vighāta) without the stinginess (mātsarya)?
The answer is:

when the fetter of wishing-for-loss regarding the dharmas to be abandoned through the vision of the Four Truths in the desire realm has not been exhausted, and the fetter of wishing-for-loss regarding the dharmas of the form and formless realms has not been exhausted—this is called having wishing-for-loss without stinginess.
What is meant by having stinginess but no failure of resolve?
The answer is:

when desire-attachment is not yet exhausted, the knowledge of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, and the fetter of stinginess regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned through mental cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) is not yet exhausted.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, the fetter of stinginess (*mātsaryasaṃyojana*) regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) is not yet exhausted.

For a disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths (*satyadarśana*), if sensual craving (*kāmarāga*) is not yet exhausted, the fetter of stinginess regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm is not yet exhausted.
This is called being stingy yet not losing one's aspiration.
What is meant by being bound by both?
The answer is:
When all the limbs and joints of the human body are bound, one is bound by both [types of fetters] regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).

When desire for the desire realm is not yet exhausted, and the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [types of fetters] regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm.
This is called being bound by both in regard to the body.
What is meant by being liberated from both?
The answer is:

When the knowledge of the origin has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion has not yet arisen, one is liberated from both categories regarding those phenomena to be abandoned by the truths of suffering and its origin; one is also liberated from both categories regarding those phenomena of the form and formless realms to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is liberated from both categories of phenomena abandoned by the truths of suffering, origin, and cessation; one is also liberated from both categories of phenomena abandoned through cultivation in the realms of form and formlessness.

A disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths is liberated from both types of factors abandoned through the vision of the four truths; they are also liberated from both types of factors abandoned through cultivation in the realms of form and formlessness.
When craving for the desire realm has been exhausted, one is liberated from both types of phenomena pertaining to the desire realm.
When craving for the form and formless realms has been exhausted, one is liberated from both types of phenomena pertaining to the form and formless realms.
This is called liberation from both.
Envy is also like this; thus ends the third [section] of the sixth "Loss of the Vow" gate.
If there is the fetter of doubt bound within the body, is there also the fetter of stinginess?
Answer: There may be doubt without stinginess.
How can there be doubt without stinginess?
Answer:

When the fetter of doubt regarding the dharmas to be abandoned through the four truths of the desire realm has not been exhausted, and the fetter of doubt regarding the dharmas of the form and formless realms has not been exhausted, this is called having doubt without stinginess.
What is meant by having stinginess but no doubt?
The answer is:

when desire-attachment is not yet exhausted, the knowledge of the path of cultivation (*bhāvanājñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, and the fetter of stinginess regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned through mental cultivation (*bhāvanāheya*) is not yet exhausted.

The knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has already arisen, but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen; thus, the fetter of stinginess (*mātsaryasaṃyojana*) regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāheya*) is not yet exhausted.

For a disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths (*satyadarśana*), sensual craving (*kāmarāga*) is not yet exhausted, and the fetter of stinginess regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation is not yet exhausted.
This is called having stinginess but no doubt.
What is meant by being bound by both?
The answer is:
When all the limbs and joints of the human body are bound, one is bound by both [types of fetters] regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).

When craving for the desire realm is not yet exhausted, and the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is bound by both [types of fetters] regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm.
This is called being bound by both.
What is meant by being liberated from both?
The answer is:

When the knowledge of the origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*kṣaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is liberated from both [types of] factors abandoned by the truth of suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) and the truth of the origin; one is liberated from both [types of] factors associated with doubt that are abandoned by the truth of cessation and the truth of the path; and one is liberated from both [types of] factors abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) belonging to the realms of form and formlessness.

When the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñāna*) has not yet arisen, one is liberated from both [the afflictions] regarding the phenomena to be abandoned through the truths of suffering, origin, and cessation; one is liberated from both [the afflictions] regarding the phenomena associated with doubt that are to be abandoned through the truth of the path; and one is liberated from both [the afflictions] regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

A disciple of the Blessed One who has realized the truths is liberated from both [the fetters] regarding those dharmas abandoned by the vision of the four truths; they are also liberated from both [the fetters] regarding those dharmas of the form and formless realms abandoned by cultivation.
When sensual craving has been exhausted, one is liberated from both aspects regarding the phenomena of the desire realm.
When craving for the form and formless realms has been exhausted, one is liberated from both aspects regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms.
This is called liberation from both.
Envy is also like this. The seventh gate on doubt is concluded.
If there is the fetter of stinginess binding within the body, is there also the fetter of envy?
Answer: It is so.
If there is envy, is there also the fetter of stinginess?
Answer: It is so.
Thus, having completed one course, one passes through the six realms of existence.
If within the body there is the bondage of past craving-ties (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also [the bondage] of the future?
Answer: It is so.
If there is a future [existence], is there also a past?
He replied:
"If that which was originally arisen has not yet ceased, then one is bound."
If it has not originally arisen, or if having originally arisen it has already ceased, then it is not bound.
If there is that which is past, is there also that which is present? Answer:
If it is present, does it also have a past?
Answer: Yes.
If that which was originally aroused is not yet exhausted, then there is bondage;
if it was not originally aroused, or if it was originally aroused but has already been exhausted, then there is no bondage.
If there is the future, is there also the present?
Answer: If it is present before one,
and there is that which is present, is there also that which is future?
He replied: "It is so.
If there is the past, is there also the future and the present?"
Answer: The future is bound to the present when it manifests before one.
If there is the future and the present, is there also the past?
The answer is:
If that which was originally aroused has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if it was not originally aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound.
If there is the future, is there also the past and the present?
The answer is:

there may be the future without the past and present; there may be the future and the past without the present; there may be the future and the present without the past; or there may be the future, the past, and the present.
What is meant by having future [tendencies] but no past or present?
The answer is:

if within one’s continuum there is the fetter of craving that has not yet been exhausted, yet it has never previously arisen, or having previously arisen has already been exhausted and does not manifest before one, this is called having the future but no past or present.
What is meant by "the future and the past exist, but the present does not"?
The answer is:

within the body, the fetter of craving has originally arisen but is not yet exhausted; although this fetter of craving for the body exists, it does not manifest in the present. This is called the future and the past existing, while the present does not.
What is meant by having future and present [fetters] but no past?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) is present within the body, yet it has never previously arisen, or if it arose, it has already been exhausted; this is called having future and present [fetters] but no past.
What is meant by "future, past, and present"?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving within the body has originally arisen but not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, this very fetter of craving for the body manifests in the present—this is called future, past, and present.
If there are [dharmas] in the past and present, are there also [dharmas] in the future?
He replied: "It is so."
If there is the present, is there also the past and the future?
The answer is:
the future is bound to the past.
If that which was originally aroused has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if it was not originally aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound.
If there is the past and the future, is there also the present?
Answer: If craving is present before one, it exhausts the six [objects].
Hatred, conceit, pride, stinginess, and envy are likewise.
If within the body there is the fetter of past ignorance, is there also that of the future?
Answer: It is so.
If there is a future [existence], is there also a past?
He replied: "It is so."
If there is the past, is there also the present?
He replied:
"If it is manifest before one."
If there is the present, is there also the past?
He replied: "It is so."
If there is the future, is there also the present?
He replied:
"If it is manifested before one."
"If there is the present, is there also the future?
He replied: "It is so."
If there is the past, is there also the future and the present?
The answer is:
the future is bound to the present, provided it manifests before one.
If there are [dharmas] in the future and the present, are there also [dharmas] in the past?
He replied: "It is so."
If there is a future [existence], is there also a past and present?
The answer is:
the past is bound to the present, provided that it manifests before one.
If there are [dharmas] of the past and present, are there also [dharmas] of the future?
He replied: "It is so."
If there is the present, are there also the past and the future?
He replied: "It is so."
If there is past and future, is there also the present?
The answer is:
if it is presently manifest, [it exists]; thus the six [periods] have been completed.
The same applies to views (*dṛṣṭi*), the vow for loss (*parāmarśa*), and doubt (*vicikitsā*).
Within a person's continuum, if there is the bondage of the past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also the past fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)? Answer:
If that which was originally aroused has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if it was not originally aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Suppose there is a past fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*); is there also a past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If that which was originally aroused has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if it was not previously aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound.
If within one's continuum there is the bondage of the past fetter of craving, is there also the fetter of future aversion?
Answer: If it has not yet been exhausted.
If there is a future fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which previously arose has not arisen, or that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Within the person, there is the bond of past craving; is there also the bond of present anger?
Answer: If it is present before one.
Suppose there is a fetter of hatred currently manifest; does there also exist a fetter of craving from the past?
Answer: If what arose previously has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if it did not arise previously, or if what arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
If within a person there is the bond of past attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also the bond of past or present aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)? Answer:

There may be the bond of past attachment without the bonds of past or present aversion; there may be the bond of past attachment along with the bond of past aversion but not the present; there may be the bond of past attachment along with the bond of present aversion but not the past; or there may be the bond of past attachment along with both the bonds of past and present aversion.
What is meant by having the past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) within the body, yet lacking the past or present fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving has previously arisen within the body and has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of ill-will has not previously arisen in this body; or, if it did previously arise, it has been exhausted and does not manifest in the present. This is called being bound by the past fetter of craving within the body, while lacking the past or present fetter of ill-will.
What is meant by "the body is bound by past fetters of craving and past fetters of ill-will, yet there are no present ones"?
The answer is:

when the fetters of craving and the fetters of ill-will within the body have arisen previously and have not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetters of ill-will do not manifest in the present within this body—this is called being bound by past fetters of craving and past fetters of ill-will within the body, with none being present.
What is meant by "the body is bound by past fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and present fetters of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), but lacks past [fetters of ill-will]"? Answer:

When the fetter of craving in the body has previously arisen and not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of ill-will in this body is present before one, while [the fetter of ill-will] either never arose originally or, having arisen, has already been exhausted—this is called the body being bound by past fetters of craving and present fetters of ill-will, but lacking past [fetters of ill-will].
What is meant by the body being bound by the fetter of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) as well as the fetters of past and present ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:

if within the body the fetters of craving and ill-will have previously arisen and not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of ill-will is currently manifest within this body, this is called the body being bound by the fetter of past craving as well as the fetters of past and present ill-will.
If there are past and present fetters of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*), is there also a past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If the fetter of craving was previously aroused and has not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which previously arose has ceased and that which arises now is exhausted, then one is not bound.
Within the body, there is the bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*); is there also the bond of future or present aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:

there may be one who is bound by the fetter of past craving but lacks the fetter of future or present ill-will; there may be one who is bound by the fetter of past craving and the fetter of future ill-will but lacks the present one; or there may be one who is bound by the fetter of past craving as well as the fetters of both future and present ill-will.
What is meant by having the past fetter of craving bound to the body, yet lacking the future and present fetters of aversion?
The answer is:

when dharmas of the form and formless realms have previously arisen and the fetter of craving has not yet been exhausted; this is called having the past fetter of craving bound to the body, without the future and present fetters of aversion.
What is meant by the body being bound by the past fetter of craving and the future fetter of aversion, yet lacking the present one?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving previously arisen within the body has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of aversion within this same body has not been exhausted but does not manifest at present—this is called the body being bound by the past fetter of craving and the future fetter of aversion, while lacking the present one.
What is meant by the body being bound by the fetter of past affection (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) as well as the fetters of future and present ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:

when the fetter of affection previously arisen within the body has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of ill-will manifests within this same body—this is called the body being bound by the fetter of past affection as well as the fetters of future and present ill-will.
If there are future and present fetters of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*), are there also past fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:
if they have previously arisen and not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by them.
If that which was originally not arisen has ceased once it arose, then one is not bound.
Within the body, there is the bond of past craving; is there also the bond of past and future ill-will?
The answer is:

there may be one who is bound by the fetter of past attachment but lacks the fetter of past or future aversion; there may be one who is bound by the fetter of past attachment and the fetter of future aversion but lacks the fetter of past aversion; or there may be one who is bound by the fetter of past attachment as well as the fetters of both past and future aversion.
What is meant by having the past fetter of craving bound to the body, yet lacking the past and future fetters of ill-will?
The answer is:

when dharmas of the form and formless realms have previously arisen and the fetter of craving has not yet been exhausted; this is called having the past fetter of craving bound to the body, yet lacking the past and future fetters of ill-will.
What is meant by "the body is bound by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and the future fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), but lacks the past [fetter of ill-will]"?
The answer is:

when craving has arisen in the body and is not yet exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of ill-will within this body has not been exhausted; provided that [ill-will] did not previously arise, or having arisen, has already ceased—this is called "the body is bound by the past fetter of craving and the future fetter of ill-will, but lacks the past [fetter of ill-will]."
What is meant by the body being bound by the fetter of past craving and the fetters of past and future ill-will?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving and the fetter of ill-will within the body have arisen previously and have not yet been exhausted, this is called the body being bound by the fetter of past craving and the fetters of past and future ill-will.
If there are past and future fetters of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*), are there also past fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If they have originally arisen and have not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by them.
If that which previously arose did not arise, or if that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
*Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha-śāstra*, Fascicle Five.

Composed by Kātyāyanīputra;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghadeva of Kaśmīr together with Zhu Fonian during the Fu Qin dynasty.

From the remainder of the *Ekottara-varga* of the *Saṃyojana-nirdeśa* in the Abhidharma: Is there, within the present body, a bond of past attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), as well as bonds of past, future, and present aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?

The answer is: there may be one who is bound by the past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) but lacks the past, future, or present fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*); or there may be one who is bound by the past fetter of craving and the future fetter of ill-will, but lacks the past or present; or there may be one who is bound by the past fetter of craving and the past and future fetters of ill-will, but lacks the present; or there may be one who is bound by the past fetter of craving and the future and present fetters of ill-will, but lacks the past; or there may be one who is bound by the past fetter of craving and the past, future, and present fetters of ill-will.
What is meant by having the bond of past attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) bound to the body, yet lacking the bonds of past, future, or present aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)? Answer:

When dharmas of the form and formless realms have previously arisen and the bond of attachment has not yet been exhausted, this is called having the bond of past attachment bound to the body, yet lacking the bonds of past, future, or present aversion.
What is meant by "the body is bound by the fetter of past craving and the fetter of future ill-will, yet lacks the fetter of past or present ill-will"?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving previously arisen within this body has not been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of ill-will within this body has also not been exhausted; or, if it was not previously arisen, or having arisen, it has already been exhausted and does not manifest before one—this is called the body being bound by the fetter of past craving and the fetter of future ill-will, while lacking the fetter of past or present [ill-will].
What is meant by "the body is bound by past fetters of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), and possesses past and future fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), but lacks the present"?
The answer is:

within the body, the fetters of attachment and aversion arose previously and have not yet been exhausted; furthermore, the fetter of aversion does not manifest in the present within this body. This is called the body being bound by past fetters of attachment and possessing past and future fetters of aversion, but lacking the present.
What is meant by "the body is bound by the past fetter of craving, and possesses the future and present fetters of ill-will, but lacks the past"?
The answer is:

when within this body the previously arisen fetter of craving has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of ill-will is present before one; or, if it was not previously arisen, or having arisen, has already been exhausted—this is called "the body is bound by the past fetter of craving, and possesses the future and present fetters of ill-will, but lacks the past."
What is meant by "the body is bound by past fetters of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) as well as past, future, and present fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)"? Answer:

When the fetters of attachment and the fetters of aversion within the body have previously arisen and not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of aversion within this body is currently manifest, this is called "the body being bound by past fetters of attachment as well as past, future, and present fetters of aversion."
If there is a fetter of malice (pratigha-saṃyojana) belonging to the past, future, or present, is there also a fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) belonging to the past?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which was originally not aroused, or that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound by anger; thus ends the section on the seven matters.
Avarice and envy are also like this.
Within the body, if there is a bond of past attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also a bond of past pride (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:
If what arose previously has not yet ceased, one is bound;
if what arose previously did not occur, or if that which arose has already ceased, one is not bound.
If there is a past fetter of conceit (*māna*), is there also a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā*)?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which previously arose has not arisen, or that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Within the body, there is the bond of past craving; is there also the bond of future conceit?
Answer: It is so.
If there is a future fetter of conceit, is there also a past fetter of craving?
Answer: If what was previously aroused has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if it was not previously aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound.
If within one's continuum there is the bondage of the past fetter of craving, is there also the present fetter of conceit?
Answer: Yes, if it is manifest at present.
If there is the present fetter of pride, is there also the past fetter of craving?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which previously arose has not arisen, or that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Within the body, there is the bond of past craving; is there also the bond of past and present conceit?
The answer is:

there may be past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) without past or present fetters of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*); there may be past fetters of craving along with past conceit but no present conceit; there may be the bondage of past fetters of craving along with present conceit but no past conceit; or there may be past fetters of craving as well as both past and present conceit.
What is meant by having the bond of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) within the body, yet no past or present conceit (*māna*)?
The answer is:

when the bond of craving previously arisen within the body has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, if conceit has not previously arisen in this body, or if it arose but has already been exhausted and does not manifest before one, this is called having the bond of past craving within the body without past or present conceit.
What is meant by having past fetters of craving and past fetters of conceit in the body, but no present ones?
The answer is:

when the fetters of craving and the fetters of conceit within the body arose previously and have not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of conceit does not manifest in this body; this is called having past fetters of craving and past fetters of conceit in the body, but none that are present.
What is meant by having the bond of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and the presence of present pride (*māna*) without the past [pride] in the body?
The answer is:

when the bond of craving previously arisen within the body has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the bond of pride is manifest in this body, provided that [the bond of pride] was not originally arisen, or if it arose, it has already been exhausted; this is called having the bond of past craving and the presence of present pride without the past [pride] in the body.
What is meant by "the body is bound by past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) as well as past and present conceit (*māna*)?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving and the fetter of conceit within the body have previously arisen and have not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of conceit within this body is currently manifest—this is called the body being bound by past fetters of craving as well as past and present conceit.
If there is the fetter of conceit (māna-saṃyojana) belonging to the past and present, is there also the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) belonging to the past?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which was originally not arisen has ceased once it arose, then one is not bound.
Within the body, there is the bond of past craving; is there also the bond of future and present conceit?
Answer: The future is bound by the present, provided it manifests before one.
If there is the fetter of conceit (māna) in the future and present, is there also the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā) in the past?
The answer is:
If what arose previously has not yet ceased, one is bound;
if what arose previously did not occur, or if that which arose has already ceased, one is not bound.
If within one's body there is the bondage of the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also the bondage of the past and future fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There is bondage in the future; as for the past, if it originally arose and has not yet been exhausted, then there is bondage.
If that which previously arose has not arisen, or that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Suppose there is past or future conceit (*māna*); is there also a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: Yes.
If what arose previously has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if what arose previously has not yet arisen, or if what arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Within the body, if there is the bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also the bond of past, future, or present conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:
There may be past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and future conceit (*māna*), but no past or present [conceit];

or there may be past fetters of craving and past and future conceit, but no present [conceit]; or there may be past fetters of craving and future and present conceit, but no past [conceit]; or there may be past fetters of craving along with past, future, and present conceit.
What is meant by having past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and future conceit (*māna*), but no past or present [conceit]?
The answer is:

when within this body the previously arisen fetters of craving have not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, conceit within this body has not yet been exhausted; yet, if [craving] was not previously arisen, or if what was arisen has already been exhausted, and moreover, conceit does not manifest in the present—this is called being bound by past fetters of craving and having future conceit, without past or present [conceit].
What is meant by being bound by past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and past and future conceit (*māna*), yet lacking present conceit?
The answer is:

when within a particular body, the previously arisen fetters of craving and conceit have not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, conceit does not manifest in that body; this is called being bound by past fetters of craving and past and future conceit, while lacking the present.
What is meant by having past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and future and present fetters of conceit (*māna*), but no past [conceit]?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving previously arisen within this body has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of conceit is currently manifest within this body; moreover, conceit had not previously arisen in this body, or if it did arise, it has already been exhausted. This is called having past fetters of craving and future and present fetters of conceit, but no past [conceit].
What is meant by having past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) as well as past, future, and present conceit (*māna*)?
The answer is:

when the fetters of craving previously arisen within this body have not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, conceit is presently manifest within this body; this is called having past fetters of craving as well as past, future, and present conceit.
If there is conceit (māna) belonging to the past, future, or present, is there also the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) belonging to the past?
Answer: If it was originally aroused and has not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which was originally not arisen has ceased, and that which arose has already ended, then the bondage of conceit is ultimately absent.
Within the body, if there is the bondage of past craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), is there also the bondage of past ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: It is so.
If there is a past fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*), is there also a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If that which was originally aroused has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if it was not originally aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Is there, within the person, the bond of past craving and the bond of future ignorance?
He replied: "It is so."
If there is a future fetter of ignorance, is there also a past fetter of craving?
Answer: If it has previously arisen and not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which was originally unarisen has ceased to arise, then one is not bound.
Within the body, there is the bond of past craving; is there also the bond of present ignorance?
Answer: If it is present before one,
and there is the fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) in the present, is there also the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) in the past?
The answer is:
If that which arose previously has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if that which arose previously has not yet arisen, or if that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
If within the body there is the bondage of the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also the past and present fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There is bondage to the past; as for the present, it exists if it is currently manifest.
If there is a bond of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past or present, is there also a bond of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not been exhausted, then one is bound.
If that which previously arose has not arisen, or that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Within the person, there is the bond of past craving; is there also the bond of future and present ignorance?
Answer: [The future fetter] is bound; [the present fetter is bound] if it is present before one.
Suppose there is the fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) in the future and present; is there also the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) in the past?
The answer is:
If that which was previously aroused has not yet ceased, one is bound;
if it was not previously aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, one is not bound.
If within a person there is the bond of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also the bond of past and future ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: It is so.
If there is the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past and future, is there also the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past?
The answer is:
if it has previously arisen and not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If it was not previously aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Within the body, there is the bond of past craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*); is there also the bond of past, future, and present ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: Those belonging to the past and future are bound; those of the present are bound if they are presently manifest.
If there is a fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) belonging to the past, future, or present, is there also a fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) belonging to the past?
Answer: If that which was originally aroused has not been exhausted, one is bound;
if it was not previously aroused, or if what was aroused has already been exhausted, one is not bound. This concludes the section on ignorance (*avidyā*).
If within one's continuum there is the bondage of past craving-fetters (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also the bondage of past view-fetters (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If they have not been exhausted.
If there is a past fetter of views, is there also a past fetter of craving?
Answer: If it was originally aroused and not yet exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which previously arose has not yet arisen, or that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Within the body, if there is past fettering by the bond of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also future fettering by the bond of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: Yes.
If it is not exhausted, and there is a future fetter of views, is there also a past fetter of craving?
Answer: Yes.
If that which was originally aroused has not yet ceased, then there is bondage;
if it was not previously aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then there is no bondage.
Within the body, if there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), is there also the present fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it is present before one.
Suppose there is a fetter of views currently manifest; is there also a fetter of craving belonging to the past?
Answer: If that which was originally aroused has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if it was not previously aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound.
If within a person there is the bondage of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also the bondage of past and present views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)? Answer:

There may be the bondage of past craving without the bondage of past and present views; there may be the bondage of past craving and past views without the present [view]; or there may be the bondage of past craving along with both past and present views.
What is meant by having the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) without the past or present fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:

when within a person the fetter of craving has previously arisen and is not yet exhausted, while the fetter of views within that same person is exhausted; this is called having the past fetter of craving without the past or present fetter of views.
What is meant by having past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and past fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), but none that are present?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving within one’s own continuum has previously arisen and not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of views within that same continuum has not yet been exhausted and does not manifest before one, this is called having past fetters of craving and past fetters of views, but none that are present.
What is meant by having past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) as well as past and present fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving previously arisen within a person has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of views manifests in that same person in the present, this is called having past fetters of craving as well as past and present fetters of views.
If there is the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past and present, is there also the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past?
The answer is:
if it was originally produced and has not yet been exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which previously arose has not yet arisen, or that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Within the body, if there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the future or present fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:

there may be past fetters of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) without future or present fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*); there may be past fetters of craving bound together with future fetters of views but not present ones; or there may be past fetters of craving along with both future and present fetters of views.
What is meant by having the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) without the future or present fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
The answer is:

when the previously arisen fetter of craving has not yet been exhausted, yet the fetter of views within that same continuum (*āśraya*) has been exhausted; this is called being bound by the past fetter of craving without the future or present fetter of views.
What is meant by having the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and the future fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), but not the present one?
The answer is:

when the fetter of craving previously arisen within this body has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the fetter of views within this body has not yet been exhausted nor is it currently manifesting, this is called being bound by the past fetter of craving and the future fetter of views, but lacking the present one.
What is meant by the bondage of past *anunaya-saṃyojana* (affectionate fetter) and the future and present *dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana* (view-fetter) within the body?
The answer is:

when the *anunaya-saṃyojana* previously arisen within the body has not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the *dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana* manifests within this very body, this is called the bondage of past *anunaya-saṃyojana* and the future and present *dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana* within the body.
If there are future and present fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), is there also a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was previously aroused and not yet exhausted, then one is bound by it.
If that which previously arose has not arisen, or that which arose has already ceased, then one is not bound.
Within the body, if there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also the past or future fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it is not exhausted,
and if there is the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past and future, is there also the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past?
Answer: If that which was originally aroused has not yet ceased, then one is bound;
if it was not previously aroused, or if that which was aroused has already ceased, then one is not bound.
If within a person there is the bondage of the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) pertaining to the past, future, and present? Answer:

There may be the bondage of the past fetter of craving without the fetter of views pertaining to the past, future, or present; or there may be the bondage of the past fetter of craving along with the fetter of views pertaining to the past and future, but not the present; or there may be the bondage of the past fetter of craving along with the fetter of views pertaining to the past, future, and present.
What is meant by "there being a bond of past craving within the body, yet no bond of past, future, or present views"?
The answer is:

when the bond of craving within the body has originally arisen and not yet been exhausted, and furthermore, the bonds of view within this body have been exhausted—this is called having a bond of past craving within the body, but no bond of past, future, or present views.
What is meant by having the bond of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and the bonds of past and future views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) within the body, but no present [view-bond]?
The answer is:
