Regarding the proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the knowledge of the truth of suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) in the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*): at the time of abandoning them through knowledge, for an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) who has reached the exhaustion of craving for the realm of form, thirty-one proclivities are abandoned through knowledge, yet the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted; for a stainless person (*vimala-pudgala*) when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna*) is present, eighteen proclivities are abandoned through knowledge, yet the fetters are not entirely exhausted.

Regarding the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the truth of the origin (*samudaya-satya*) within the form realm (*rūpadhātu*): at the time of the knowledge of abandonment (*prahāṇa-jñāna*), for an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) who has reached the exhaustion of craving for the form realm, thirty-one latent tendencies are known through the knowledge of abandonment, yet the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted. For a stainless person (*vimalapudgala*) in whom the knowledge of the unknown (*anājñāta-ājñāna*) is present, twelve latent tendencies are known through the knowledge of abandonment, yet the fetters are not entirely exhausted.
The same applies to the underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the truth of cessation.

Regarding the underlying tendencies abandoned through the truth of the path in the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*): when one attains the knowledge of abandonment (*prahāṇajñāna*), an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) who has reached the exhaustion of craving for the realm of form abandons thirty-one underlying tendencies, yet does not completely exhaust the fetters (*saṃyojana*) through that knowledge of abandonment. When a stainless person (*vimalapudgala*) brings the knowledge of the path of seeing (*mārgajñāna*) into manifestation, they abandon fourteen underlying tendencies and the three fetters are eternally exhausted.

Regarding the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through cultivation in the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), at the time of the knowledge of abandonment (*prahāṇajñāna*): for an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) who has reached the exhaustion of craving for the realm of form, thirty-one latent dispositions are known as abandoned, yet the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted; for a stainless person (*vimalapudgala*), three latent dispositions are known as abandoned, yet the fetters are not entirely exhausted.

Regarding the proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the truth of suffering (*duḥkhasatya*) in the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*): at the time of abandoning them through the knowledge of abandonment (*prahāṇajñāna*), if desire for the form realm (*rūparāga*) has not yet been exhausted and the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhānvayajñāna*) is present, eighteen proclivities are abandoned through the knowledge of abandonment, yet the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted.

If desire for the form realm has already been exhausted and the subsequent knowledge of suffering is present, nine proclivities are abandoned through the knowledge of abandonment, yet the fetters are not entirely exhausted.

Regarding the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) of the formless realm to be abandoned by the truth of origination (*samudayasatya*): at the time of abandoning them through the knowledge of abandonment (*prahāṇajñāna*), if craving for the form realm (*rūparāga*) has not yet been exhausted and the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudayānvayajñāna*) is present, twelve latent tendencies are abandoned through the knowledge of abandonment, yet the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted.

If craving for the form realm has already been exhausted and the subsequent knowledge of origination is present, six latent tendencies are abandoned through the knowledge of abandonment, yet the fetters are not entirely exhausted.
The same applies to the proclivities (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the truth of cessation.

Regarding the proclivities abandoned through the truth of the path in the formless realm: at the time of the knowledge of abandonment, when desire for the form realm (*rūparāga*) has not yet been exhausted and the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna*) is present, fourteen proclivities are abandoned through knowledge and the three fetters (*saṃyojana*) are eternally exhausted.

When desire for the form realm has already been exhausted and the subsequent knowledge of the path is present, seven proclivities are abandoned through knowledge and the three fetters are eternally exhausted.

Regarding the proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through cultivation in the formless realm: at the time of the knowledge of abandonment, one reaches the exhaustion of craving for the formless realm; thus, there is the knowledge of abandonment of the three proclivities and the permanent exhaustion of the three fetters (*saṃyojana*). This concludes the nine gates of the knowledge of abandonment.

When the faculty of the eye is fully realized, for an ordinary person who has reached the exhaustion of craving for the realm of form (*rūparāga*), thirty-one proclivities (*anuśaya*) are fully realized, yet the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not all exhausted; for a stainless person (*vimala*), three proclivities are fully realized, yet the fetters are not all exhausted; when one attains Arhatship, ninety-eight proclivities are fully realized and the nine fetters are eternally exhausted.
As with the eye faculty (*cakṣur-indriya*), so it is with the ear, nose, tongue, and body faculties;

the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*), ear, nose, tongue, and body bases; the form, sound, and tangible-object bases (*spraṣṭavya-āyatana*); the eye-sphere (*cakṣur-dhātu*), ear, nose, tongue, and body spheres; the form-sphere, sound, and tangible-object spheres;

the aggregate of form (*rūpa-skandha*) and the aggregate of the predominance of form (*rūpādhipati-skandha*); the earth element (*pṛthivī-dhātu*) up to the space element (*ākāśa-dhātu*); and form-phenomena (*rūpa-dharma*) and visible phenomena (*sanidarśana-dharma*).

When one realizes the cessation of the following: obstructive phenomena (*sapratigha-dharma*), phenomena bound to the realm of form (*rūpāvacara-dharma*), the fourth dhyāna, loving-kindness (*maitrī*), compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), equanimity (*upekṣā*), the pure liberation (*śubha-vimokṣa*),
the latter four bases of mastery (*abhibhv-āyatana*), the eight bases of totality (*kṛtsnāyatana*), and the knowledge of others' minds (*paracittajñāna*)—

if it is an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) who has reached the exhaustion of craving for the realm of form (*rūpa-rāga-kṣaya*), they realize the cessation of thirty-one underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*), yet they have not completely severed all fetters (*saṃyojana*).
In the case of a person free from defilements (*vimala*), when the three underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) are fully exhausted and realized, the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not yet entirely exhausted;
however, upon attaining arhatship, ninety-eight underlying tendencies are fully exhausted and realized, and the nine fetters are eternally exhausted.

When the faculty of mind (*manendriya*) is fully realized, one attains the realization of the exhaustion of the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) and the eternal cessation of the nine fetters (*saṃyojana*).

As it is with the faculty of mind, so it is with the faculty of life (*jīvitendriya*), the faculty of equanimity (*upekṣendriya*), the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom;

the mental base (*manāyatana*), the dharma-base (*dharmāyatana*), and the mental-consciousness base (*manovijñānāyatana*); the aggregates of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; and so forth.
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregates of perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the element of consciousness;

formless phenomena, invisible phenomena, non-obstructive phenomena, phenomena with outflows, conditioned phenomena, phenomena of the past, future, and present, wholesome phenomena, indeterminate phenomena, phenomena bound to the formless realm, and phenomena that are neither-learner-nor-non-learner.
When one realizes the cessation of the factors to be abandoned by reflection, the Truth of Suffering, the Truth of Origination, the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,
the liberation of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the liberation of cessation, and conventional knowledge, one attains arhatship,
realizes the exhaustion of the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*), and brings about the eternal extinction of the nine fetters (*saṃyojana*).

When the male faculty and female faculty are fully realized: for an ordinary person who has reached the exhaustion of sensual desire, thirty-six underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) are fully realized and the three fetters (*saṃyojana*) are eternally exhausted; upon attaining the fruit of *anāgāmin*, ninety-two underlying tendencies are fully realized and six fetters—namely, stinginess, envy, and ill-will—are eternally exhausted, which constitutes the third stage of the path; upon attaining the fruit of *arhat*, ninety-eight underlying tendencies are fully realized and nine fetters are eternally exhausted.

Just as with the male faculty and the female faculty, so it is when one realizes the cessation of the painful faculty, the faculty of grief, the odor-base and taste-base, the nose-consciousness-base and tongue-consciousness-base, the odor-element and taste-element, unwholesome phenomena, and phenomena bound to the desire realm: an ordinary person who reaches the exhaustion of sensual craving realizes the cessation of thirty-six proclivities (*anuśaya*) and the permanent extinction of the three fetters (*saṃyojana*); one who attains the fruit of non-returner (*anāgāmin*) realizes the cessation of ninety-two proclivities and the permanent extinction of six fetters; one who attains arhatship realizes the cessation of ninety-eight proclivities and the permanent extinction of nine fetters.

When one realizes the exhaustion of the faculty of pleasure (*sukhendriya*), one reaches the exhaustion of craving for the Subhakṛtsna Heaven; yet at that very moment of realizing the exhaustion of the faculty of pleasure, the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted. Upon attaining the fruit of Arhatship, one realizes the exhaustion of the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) and the nine fetters (*grantha*) are forever extinguished.

When one realizes the exhaustion of the faculty of joy (*somanassindriya*), one reaches the exhaustion of craving for the Ābhāsvara Heaven; yet, while that faculty of joy is realized as exhausted, the underlying fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not all exhausted. When one realizes the exhaustion of the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*), one attains arhatship and the nine fetters (*saṃyojana*) are eternally exhausted.

When one realizes the exhaustion of the eye-consciousness-element, ear-consciousness-element, and body-consciousness-element, reaching the exhaustion of craving up to the Brahma-heaven, although these three consciousness-elements are realized as exhausted, the fetters are not yet entirely exhausted; however, upon attaining Arhatship, one realizes the exhaustion of all ninety-eight underlying tendencies (anuśaya) and the eternal exhaustion of the nine fetters (saṃyojana).

When one realizes the exhaustion of the dharmas to be abandoned by the vision of the truths, one attains the fruit of *srotāpanna* through the realization of the exhaustion of eighty-eight *anuśayas* and the permanent cessation of the three fetters; one attains the fruit of *sakṛdāgāmin* through the realization of the exhaustion of eighty-eight *anuśayas* and the permanent cessation of the three fetters; one attains the fruit of *anāgāmin* through the realization of the exhaustion of ninety-two *anuśayas* and the permanent cessation of the six fetters; and one attains the fruit of *arhat* through the realization of the exhaustion of ninety-eight *anuśayas* and the permanent cessation of the nine fetters.

Regarding the first dhyāna among the dhyānas: when one fully realizes it, up to the point where craving for the first dhyāna is exhausted, although that first dhyāna is fully realized, the fetters (saṃyojana) are not yet entirely exhausted; however, upon attaining arhatship, one fully realizes the exhaustion of all ninety-eight underlying tendencies (anuśaya), and the nine fetters (saṃyojana) are forever exhausted.

When one fully realizes the second dhyāna, one reaches the exhaustion of craving for the second dhyāna; yet, while fully realizing that exhaustion of the second dhyāna, the fetters (saṃyojana) are not entirely exhausted. Only upon attaining arhatship does one fully realize the exhaustion of the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (anuśaya), whereby the nine fetters are forever extinguished.
It is likewise for the joy [of the first dhyāna], the first and second liberations, and the first four spheres of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*).

When one fully realizes the third dhyāna, one reaches the exhaustion of craving for the third dhyāna; yet, although that third dhyāna is fully realized, the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted. Upon attaining arhatship, one fully realizes the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) and the nine fetters are forever exhausted.

When one fully realizes the sphere of infinite space within the formless realm, one reaches the exhaustion of craving for the sphere of infinite space; yet, while fully realizing that very sphere of infinite space, the fetters are not entirely exhausted. Upon attaining arhatship, one fully realizes the exhaustion of the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (anuśaya) and the nine fetters (saṃyojana) are forever extinguished.
It is likewise for the liberation of the sphere of infinite space and the entry into the sphere of infinite space.

When one fully realizes the sphere of infinite consciousness (*vijñānānantyāyatana*), one reaches the exhaustion of craving for the sphere of infinite consciousness; yet, while fully realizing that exhaustion of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted. Upon attaining arhatship, one fully realizes the exhaustion of the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) and the nine fetters are forever extinguished.
The same applies to the liberation of the sphere of consciousness and the entry into the sphere of consciousness.

When one realizes the exhaustion of the sphere of nothingness, one reaches the exhaustion of craving for the sphere of nothingness; yet, while realizing that exhaustion of the sphere of nothingness, the fetters are not entirely exhausted. Upon attaining arhatship, one realizes the exhaustion of the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) and the nine fetters (*saṃyojana*) are forever extinguished.
The same applies to the liberation of the sphere of nothingness (*ākiṃcanyāyatana-vimokṣa*).

When one realizes the exhaustion of the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*) among the fetters, the knowledge of the suffering yet to be known (*duḥkhe 'nvaya-jñāna*) manifests; eighteen latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) are realized as exhausted, though not all fetters are completely exhausted. Upon attaining the fruits of *srotāpanna*, *sakṛdāgāmin*, *anāgāmin*, or *arhat*, ninety-eight latent tendencies are realized as exhausted and the nine fetters are eternally extinguished.

Among the lower fetters, when one realizes the exhaustion of the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*)—specifically the view of a self-identity and the view of extremes (*antagrāhadṛṣṭi*)—the "unknown-to-be-known" knowledge regarding suffering (*duḥkhe 'jñāsyāmīti-jñāna*) manifests. At that time, eighteen underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) are realized as exhausted, yet not all fetters (*saṃyojana*) are completely exhausted. Upon attaining the fruits of *srotāpanna*, *sakṛdāgāmin*, *anāgāmin*, or *arhat*, ninety-eight underlying tendencies are realized as exhausted and the nine fetters are eternally extinguished.

When the fetters of dogmatic attachment to precepts and rituals (*śīlavrata-parāmarśa*) and doubt (*vicikitsā*) are fully realized as extinguished, one attains the fruits of *srotāpanna*, *sakṛdāgāmin*, *anāgāmin*, or *arhat*; at that time, the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) are fully realized as extinguished and the nine fetters (*saṃyojana*) are eternally exhausted.

When one fully realizes the realization of the stream of views, the yoke of views, the clinging to precepts and observances, the clinging to views, the bodily fetter of the theft of precepts, the bodily fetter of the view of self, the theft of precepts and doubt among the lower fetters, wrong view, the clinging to views, and the theft of precepts among the views, as well as the latent tendency of views and the latent tendency of doubt among the latent tendencies, and the fetter of views, the fetter of resentment, and the fetter of doubt among the fetters—at that time of full realization, one attains the fruit of Stream-enterer, Once-returner, Non-returner, or Arhatship; the ninety-eight latent tendencies are fully realized as exhausted, and the nine fetters are eternally extinguished.

When one realizes the exhaustion of greed, hatred, delusion, and the outflow of desire (*kāma-āsrava*), an ordinary person reaches the end of sensual craving; they realize the exhaustion of thirty-six proclivities (*anuśaya*) and the permanent extinction of the three fetters (*saṃyojana*). One who attains the fruit of Non-returning (*anāgāmin*) realizes the exhaustion of ninety-two proclivities and the permanent extinction of six fetters. One who attains the fruit of Arhatship realizes the exhaustion of ninety-eight proclivities and the permanent extinction of nine fetters.

In this way, when one realizes the exhaustion of the flood of desire (*kāma-ogha*), the yoke of desire (*kāma-yoga*), the craving of desire (*kāma-tṛṣṇā*), the bodily bond of craving for desire (*kāmacchanda-kāyagrantha*) and the bodily bond of ill-will (*vyāpāda-kāyagrantha*); among the hindrances (*nīvaraṇa*), greed, ill-will, sloth-and-torpor, and restlessness; among the fetters (*saṃyojana*), the fetters of ill-will, stinginess, and envy; among the lower fetters (*avarabhāgīya*), greed and ill-will; among the cravings of the body (*kāmarāga*), the craving of nose and tongue contact; among the underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*), the underlying tendencies of greed and ill-will; and among the knots (*grantha*), the knots of ill-will, stinginess, and envy—at the time of such realization: An ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) reaches the exhaustion of craving for desire and realizes the exhaustion of thirty-six underlying tendencies, with the three fetters forever exhausted, thereby attaining the fruit of Non-returner (*anāgāmiphala*) through the realization of the exhaustion of ninety-two underlying tendencies and the forever-exhaustion of six fetters. One attains the fruit of Arhatship (*arhattvaphala*) through the realization of the exhaustion of ninety-eight underlying tendencies and the forever-exhaustion of nine fetters.

When the outflow of the taints (*āsrava*) and the outflow of ignorance (*avidyā-āsrava*) are fully realized, one attains the fruit of Arhatship; the ninety-eight proclivities (*anuśaya*) are fully realized and the nine fetters (*saṃyojana*) are eternally exhausted.

When the flow, the intermediate flow, and the flow of ignorance; the yoke, the intermediate yoke, and the yoke of ignorance; the fetter of self-love, the fetter of pride; the craving for mental contact, the craving for existence, the proclivity of pride, and the proclivity of ignorance; and the fetter of craving, the fetter of pride, and the fetter of ignorance are fully realized, one attains the fruit of Arhatship; the ninety-eight proclivities are fully realized and the nine fetters are eternally exhausted.

When the hindrance of doubt (*vicikitsā-nīvaraṇa*) is fully realized: for an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) who has reached the exhaustion of sensual desire, thirty-six underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) are fully realized and the three fetters (*saṃyojana*) are eternally exhausted; when the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path (*mārga-dharmajñāna*) is present before a stainless person (*anāsrava-pudgala*), eight underlying tendencies are fully realized but the fetters are not yet entirely exhausted; upon attaining the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpanna-phala*) up to the fruit of arhatship (*arhat-phala*), ninety-eight underlying tendencies are fully realized and the nine fetters are eternally exhausted.

When one realizes the exhaustion of craving for eye, ear, and body-contact, one reaches the exhaustion of craving up to the Brahma-heaven; at that very moment, through the realization of the exhaustion of those three cravings, the fetters are not yet entirely exhausted, yet one attains the fruit of Arhatship by realizing the exhaustion of the ninety-eight underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) and the eternal exhaustion of the nine fetters (*saṃyojana*).

Among the ninety-eight *anuśayas*, when the *anuśayas* to be abandoned through the vision of the truth of suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) in the desire realm are fully realized: for an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) who has reached the exhaustion of desire for the realm of sensuality, thirty-six *anuśayas* are fully realized and the three fetters (*saṃyojana*) are eternally exhausted; for a stainless person (*vimala-pudgala*) when the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*) is present, ten *anuśayas* are fully realized but the fetters are not yet entirely exhausted; and upon attaining the fruit of a stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*) up to the fruit of an arhat, all ninety-eight *anuśayas* are fully realized and the nine fetters are eternally exhausted.

When one realizes the cessation of the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the Truth of Origination within the desire realm, an ordinary person who has reached the exhaustion of desire attains the realization of the cessation of thirty-six latent dispositions and the permanent extinction of the three fetters (*saṃyojana*). For a stainless person (*vimala-pudgala*), when the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna*) is present, they realize the cessation of seven latent dispositions, though not all fetters are yet exhausted. Upon attaining the fruit of a stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*) up to the fruit of an arhat, one realizes the cessation of ninety-eight latent dispositions and the permanent extinction of the nine fetters.
The same applies to the proclivities (*anuśaya*) abandoned by the truth of cessation (*nirodha-satya*).

When the proclivities abandoned by the truth of the path (*mārga-satya*) in the desire realm are fully realized, an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) who has reached the exhaustion of sensual craving realizes thirty-six proclivities and the three fetters (*saṃyojana*) are forever exhausted. For one without taints (*vimala*), when the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path (*mārga-dharmajñāna*) is present, eight proclivities are realized but the fetters are not yet entirely exhausted; upon attaining the fruit of stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*) up to the fruit of arhatship, ninety-eight proclivities are realized and the nine fetters are forever exhausted.

When one realizes the extinction of the proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm: for an ordinary person who has reached the exhaustion of sensual craving, thirty-six proclivities are realized as extinguished and the three fetters (*saṃyojana*) are eternally exhausted; for one who attains the fruit of *anāgāmin*, ninety-two proclivities are realized as extinguished and six fetters are eternally exhausted; for one who attains the fruit of *arhat*, ninety-eight proclivities are realized as extinguished and nine fetters are eternally exhausted.

When the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the truth of suffering in the form realm are fully realized: for an ordinary person who has reached the exhaustion of desire for the form realm, thirty-one latent tendencies are fully realized, yet the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not all exhausted; for a stainless person (*vimala-pudgala*) when the "subsequent knowledge of suffering" (*duḥkhe 'nvaya-jñāna*) is present, eighteen latent tendencies are fully realized, yet the fetters are not all exhausted; upon attaining the fruit of stream-entry up to the fruit of arhatship, ninety-eight latent tendencies are fully realized and the nine fetters are eternally exhausted.

When one realizes the exhaustion of the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned by the Truth of Origination in the form realm, an ordinary person who has reached the end of craving for the form realm realizes the exhaustion of thirty-one latent tendencies, yet does not completely exhaust all fetters (*saṃyojana*). For a stainless person (*vimala-pudgala*), when the knowledge of the unknown regarding origination (*samudaye 'jñāta-jñāna*) is present, they realize the exhaustion of twelve latent tendencies, yet do not completely exhaust all fetters. Upon attaining the fruit of Stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*) up to the fruit of Arhatship, one realizes the exhaustion of ninety-eight latent tendencies and the fetters are forever exhausted.
It is likewise when one realizes the exhaustion of the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the truth of cessation (*nirodha-satya*).

When one realizes the exhaustion of the latent tendencies to be abandoned by the truth of the path (*mārga-satya*) pertaining to the form realm (*rūpa-dhātu*), an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) who has reached the exhaustion of desire for the form realm realizes the exhaustion of thirty-one latent tendencies, yet does not fully exhaust all fetters (*saṃyojana*). When a stainless person (*vimalapudgala*) brings the knowledge of the path of the unknown (*anvaya-jñāna*) into presence, they realize the exhaustion of fourteen latent tendencies and the eternal exhaustion of the three fetters, attaining the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpanna-phala*) up to the fruit of arhatship (*arhat-phala*), wherein they realize the exhaustion of ninety-eight latent tendencies and the eternal exhaustion of the nine fetters.

When one realizes the exhaustion of the proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through cultivation in the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), an ordinary person who has reached the exhaustion of desire for the realm of form realizes the exhaustion of thirty-one proclivities, yet does not fully exhaust all fetters (*saṃyojana*). A stainless person (*vimala*) realizes the exhaustion of three proclivities, yet does not fully exhaust all fetters. Upon attaining the fruit of Arhatship, one realizes the exhaustion of ninety-eight proclivities and the fetters are eternally exhausted.

When one realizes the extinction of the proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the Truth of Suffering in the formless realm, the "subsequent knowledge of suffering" (*duḥkhe 'nvayajñāna*) manifests; eighteen proclivities are realized as extinguished, yet the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted. Upon attaining the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpanna*) up to the fruit of arhatship, ninety-eight proclivities are realized as extinguished and the nine fetters are forever exhausted.

When one realizes the exhaustion of the proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the truth of origination within the formless realm, the knowledge of the unknown regarding origination (*samudayānvayajñāna*) manifests; twelve proclivities are realized as exhausted, yet the fetters (*saṃyojana*) are not entirely exhausted. Upon attaining the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpanna*) up to the fruit of arhatship, ninety-eight proclivities are realized as exhausted and the nine fetters are eternally exhausted.
The same applies to those [defilements] abandoned through the truth of cessation.

When one realizes the exhaustion of the proclivities (anuśaya) to be abandoned through the truth of the path in the formless realm, one attains the fruit of stream-entry up to the fruit of arhatship; the ninety-eight proclivities are realized as exhausted and the nine fetters (saṃyojana) are eternally eliminated.

When one realizes the exhaustion of the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through cultivation in the formless realm, one attains Arhatship; having realized the exhaustion of the ninety-eight latent tendencies, one realizes the eternal exhaustion of the nine fetters (*saṃyojana*). This concludes the tenth gate.
The Fourth Chapter on the Ten Gates of the Saṃyojana-skandha is completed. The Sanskrit original consists of one thousand sixty ślokas and twelve characters.
