Chapter Seven: The Section on Conditions (Paccayavāra). Part One of the First Section on Roots (Mūlakhandhaka). Regarding "causes" (hetu), these are the various conditions; they should be arranged in successive order: five, three, and four; four together with eight; eight equals eight; and eight also equals four.
If the various faculties have the past as their cause, do those faculties have the past as their object?
Conversely, if the various faculties have the past as their object, do those faculties have the past as their cause?

Regarding the various faculties that have the future as their cause, the present as their cause; that which is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate as their cause; that which is bound to the desire realm, the form realm, the formless realm, or is unbound as their cause; that which is of the learner, the non-learner, or neither-learner-nor-non-learner as their cause; and that which is abandoned by seeing the truths, abandoned by cultivation, or not to be abandoned as their cause—do those faculties have the unconditioned (the unceasing) as their object?
If various faculties have non-abandonment (*aprahāṇa*) as their object, do those faculties have non-abandonment as their cause? [End of Section 5.3.

Regarding those faculties that have the abandonment through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) as their cause, do those faculties have the abandonment through the vision of suffering as their object?

If various faculties have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering?

If various faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya*), cessation (*nirodha*), or the path (*mārga*), do those faculties have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the path?

If the various faculties have as their object that which is abandoned by the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by the path of seeing? [End of Chapter Four.

Do the various faculties that have as their cause that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) have as their object that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*)?

If the various faculties have suffering-dharma-knowledge-abandonment (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*) as their object, do those faculties have seeing-suffering-abandonment (*darśana-duḥkha-prahātavya*) as their cause?
And if the various faculties have seeing-suffering-abandonment as their cause, do those faculties have suffering-subsequent-knowledge-abandonment (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*) as their object?

If the various faculties have suffering as their object and are abandoned by the knowledge of the unknown regarding suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna), do those faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya)?

If the various faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by the vision of origin, the vision of cessation, or the vision of the path, do those faculties have the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path (mārga-dharma-jñāna) as their object and are abandoned thereby?

If the various faculties have the path-dharma-knowledge (mārga-dharmajñāna) as their object and are abandoned by that [knowledge], do those faculties have the vision-of-the-path (darśanamārga) as their cause and are abandoned by that [vision]?

If the various faculties have the vision-of-the-path as their cause and are abandoned by that [vision], do those faculties have the subsequent-knowledge-of-the-path (mārgānvayajñāna) as their object and are abandoned by that [knowledge]?

If the various faculties have the path-unknown-knowledge-abandonment (*mārgājñāna-ajñāsyāmīndriya-prahātavya*) as their object, do those faculties have the path-seeing-abandonment (*darśanamārga-prahātavya*) as their cause? [The fourfold and eightfold sets are concluded.

Regarding the various faculties that have the suffering-dharma-knowledge-abandonment (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*) as their cause, do those faculties have the suffering-dharma-knowledge-abandonment as their object?
If the various faculties have suffering-dharma-knowledge-abandonment (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*) as their object, do those faculties have suffering-dharma-knowledge-abandonment as their cause?

If the various faculties have suffering-subsequent-knowledge-abandonment (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*) as their cause, do those faculties have suffering-subsequent-knowledge-abandonment as their object?

If the various faculties have suffering as their object and are abandoned by the knowledge of the unknown regarding suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*), do those faculties have suffering as their cause and are abandoned by the knowledge of the unknown regarding suffering?

If the various faculties have the knowledge of the dharma regarding origin, cessation, and the path as their cause and are abandoned by that knowledge, do those faculties have the path as their object and are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path?

If the various faculties have the path-dharma-knowledge (mārga-dharma-jñāna) as their object and are abandoned by the path-dharma-knowledge, do those faculties have the path-dharma-knowledge as their cause and are abandoned by the path-dharma-knowledge?

If the various faculties have the path-subsequent-knowledge (mārga-anvaya-jñāna) as their cause and are abandoned by the path-subsequent-knowledge, do those faculties have the path-subsequent-knowledge as their object and are abandoned by the path-subsequent-knowledge?

If the various faculties have the path-unknown-knowledge-abandonment (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*) as their object, do those faculties have the path-unknown-knowledge-abandonment as their cause? [The eightfold combination is concluded.

Regarding the various faculties that have the suffering-dharma-knowledge-abandonment (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*) as their cause, do those faculties have the seeing-of-suffering-abandonment (*darśana-duḥkha-prahātavya*) as their object?

If the various faculties have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*)?

And if the various faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering?

If various faculties have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe 'nvaya-jñāna*)?

If various faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned through the dharma-knowledge of origin, cessation, and the path (*samudaya-nirodha-mārga-dharma-jñāna*), do those faculties have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*)?

If various faculties have as their object that which is abandoned by the path of seeing (*darśanamārga-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path (*mārgadharmajñāna-prahātavya*)?

If various faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their object that which is abandoned by the path of seeing?

If the various faculties have as their object that which is abandoned by the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the unknown path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*)?
[End of Section 8.4]. May the meaning of this chapter be fully expounded.
If the various faculties have the past as their cause, do those faculties have the past as their object?
Answer:

Some faculties have the past as their cause and take the past as their object, take the future as their object, take the present as their object, take the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) as their object, or have no object.
How do faculties have the past as their cause and take the past as their object?
Answer:
The faculties have the past as their cause and the past as their object; furthermore, the future and present faculties have the past as their cause and the past as their object.
How do the faculties have the past as their cause and the future as their object?
Answer:
The faculties that are past have the future as their object; furthermore, the faculties that are future or present have the past as their cause and the future as their object.
How do the faculties have the past as their cause and the present as their object?
Answer:
The faculties that are past have the present as their object. Furthermore, the faculties that are future or present have the past as their cause and the present as their object.
How is it that a faculty has the past as its cause and the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) as its object?

Answer: There are faculties that are past and have the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) as their object; furthermore, there are faculties that are future or present and have the past as their cause and the unconditioned as their object.
What are the faculties that have the past as their cause but no object?
Answer: Are the faculties (indriya) that have past phenomena as their object caused by past phenomena?
Furthermore, if the faculties have past phenomena as their object, are those faculties caused by past phenomena?
Answer: Some faculties have the past as their object, having the past as their cause, the future as their cause, or the present as their cause.
What is meant by a faculty that has the past as its object and the past as its cause?
Answer:

The faculties (indriya) that have the past as their object (ālambana) and the past as their cause (hetu); furthermore, those faculties that are future or present have the past as their cause and the past as their object.
What are the faculties that have the past as their object and the future as their cause?
Answer: The faculties (indriya) that are future have the past as their object.
How can a faculty have the past as its object while being conditioned by the present?
Answer:
The faculties that are present have the past as their object. Furthermore, the faculties that are future have the present as their cause and the past as their object.
When the faculties have the future as their cause, do those faculties have the future as their object?
Answer:

Some faculties have the future as their cause, and they take the future as their object, the past as their object, the present as their object, the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) as their object, or have no object.
What is meant by a faculty that has the future as its cause and takes the future as its object?
Answer: The faculties that are future have the future as their object.
How can a faculty that has the future as its cause have the past as its object?
Answer: The faculties (*indriya*) that are future have the past as their object (*ālambana*).
How can a faculty that has the future as its cause have the present as its object?
Answer: The faculties (indriya) that are future have the present as their object (ālambana).
How can a faculty be conditioned by the future while having the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) as its object?
Answer: The faculties (*indriya*) that are future have the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) as their object.
How can a faculty be future, have no object, and yet be the cause [of another]?
Answer: Are the faculties (indriya) that have future dharmas as their objects caused by future dharmas?
Furthermore, if the faculties have future dharmas as their objects, are those faculties caused by future dharmas?
Answer: Some faculties have the future as their object (ālambana), having the future as their cause (hetu), the past as their cause, or the present as their cause.
What is meant by a faculty that has the future as its object and has the future as its cause?
Answer: The faculties (indriya) that are future have the future as their object (ālambana).
How can a faculty that has the future as its object have the past as its cause (hetu)?
Answer:
The faculties (*indriya*) of the past take the future as their object. Furthermore, the faculties of the future and present have the past as their cause and the future as their object.
How is it that a faculty has the future as its object and the present as its cause?
Answer:
The faculties that are present have the future as their object. Furthermore, the faculties that are future have the present as their cause and the future as their object.
As for those faculties that have the present as their cause, do those faculties have the present as their object?
Answer:
Some faculties have the present as their cause, and they take the present as their object, the past as their object, the future as their object, the unconditioned as their object, or have no object.
What is meant by a faculty that has the present as its cause and takes the present as its object?
Answer: The faculties that are present have the present as their object; furthermore, the faculties that are future have the present as their cause and the present as their object.
How is it that a faculty has the present as its cause and the past as its object?
Answer:
The faculties are present while taking the past as their object. Furthermore, the future faculties have the present as their cause and take the past as their object.
How is it that the faculties have the present as their cause and take the future as their object?
Answer:
The faculties (indriya) that are present take the future as their object; furthermore, the faculties that are future have the present as their cause and take the future as their object.
How is it that a faculty has the present as its cause and takes the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) as its object?

Answer: The faculties (indriya) are present and take the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) as their object; furthermore, the future faculties have the present as their cause and take the unconditioned as their object.
What are the faculties that have the present as their cause but no object?
Answer: Are the faculties (indriya) that have no object-condition (ālambana-pratyaya) caused by present phenomena?
Furthermore, if the faculties have a present object, are those faculties caused by the present?
Answer: Some faculties have the present as their object (ālambana), with causes (hetu) in the present, causes in the past, or causes in the future.
What are the faculties that have the present as their object and have causes in the present?
Answer: The faculties that are present have the present as their object; furthermore, those faculties that are future have the present as their cause and the present as their object.
How is it that a faculty has the present as its object and the past as its cause?
Answer:
The faculties (indriya) that are past have the present as their object; furthermore, the faculties that are future or present have the past as their cause and the present as their object.
How is it that a faculty has the present as its object and the future as its cause?
Answer: The faculties that are future have the present as their object; this concludes the first three [sections].
Regarding those faculties whose cause is wholesome, do those faculties have a wholesome object?
Answer:
Some faculties have a wholesome cause and take a wholesome object, an unwholesome object, an indeterminate object, or have no object.
What are the faculties that have a wholesome cause and take a wholesome object?
Answer: The faculties are wholesome when they have wholesome objects; furthermore, the faculties that are indeterminate have wholesome causes and wholesome objects.
How is it that a faculty has a wholesome cause but an unwholesome object?

Answer: There are faculties that have wholesome roots as their cause but take unwholesome objects; furthermore, there are faculties that are indeterminate (avyākṛta) yet have wholesome roots as their cause and take unwholesome objects.
What are the faculties that have wholesome roots as their cause and take indeterminate objects?
Answer: The faculties have wholesome conditions that are indeterminate; furthermore, the faculties that are themselves indeterminate have wholesome causes and indeterminate conditions.
What are the faculties that have wholesome causes but no conditions?
Answer: Are the faculties (indriya) that lack an object-condition (ālambana-pratyaya) caused by wholesome dharmas?
Furthermore, if the faculties have wholesome objects, are those faculties caused by wholesome [dharmas]?
Answer: Some faculties have the wholesome as their object, and are caused by the wholesome, caused by the unwholesome, or caused by the indeterminate.
What are the faculties that have the wholesome as their object and are caused by the wholesome?
Answer: The faculties are wholesome when they have wholesome objects; furthermore, the faculties are indeterminate when they have wholesome causes and wholesome objects.
How is it that the faculties have wholesome objects but have unwholesome causes?
Answer: There are faculties that are unwholesome while having wholesome objects; furthermore, there are faculties that are indeterminate while having unwholesome causes and wholesome objects.
What are the faculties that have wholesome objects and indeterminate causes?

Answer: The faculties that are indeterminate (*avyākṛta*) take the wholesome (*kuśala*) as their object. Furthermore, the faculties that are unwholesome (*akuśala*) have the indeterminate as their cause and take the wholesome as their object. [End of section on the wholesome.
Now, regarding those faculties that have the unwholesome as their cause, do those faculties take the unwholesome as their object?
Answer: Some faculties have unwholesome roots as their cause, and they take as their object (ālambana) the unwholesome, the wholesome, the indeterminate, or have no object.
How do faculties have unwholesome roots as their cause and take the unwholesome as their object?
Answer: There are faculties that are unwholesome and have unwholesome objects; furthermore, there are faculties that are indeterminate, have unwholesome causes, and have unwholesome objects.
What are the faculties that have unwholesome causes and wholesome objects?

Answer: There are faculties that are unwholesome while having wholesome objects; furthermore, there are faculties that are indeterminate while being caused by the unwholesome and having wholesome objects.
How are there faculties that are caused by the unwholesome and have indeterminate objects?
Answer: There are faculties that are unwholesome with neutral objects; furthermore, there are faculties that are neutral, having unwholesome causes and neutral objects.
What are the faculties that have unwholesome causes but no objects?
Answer: Are there faculties that lack an object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) yet have unwholesome phenomena as their cause?
Furthermore, if faculties have unwholesome phenomena as their object, do those faculties have unwholesome phenomena as their cause?
Answer: Some faculties have unwholesome objects and are caused by the unwholesome, caused by the wholesome, or caused by the indeterminate.
What are the faculties that have unwholesome objects and are caused by the unwholesome?
Answer: There are faculties that are unwholesome and have unwholesome objects; furthermore, there are faculties that are indeterminate, have unwholesome causes, and have unwholesome objects.
What are the faculties that have unwholesome objects and have wholesome causes?
Answer: There are faculties that have wholesome objects but are unwholesome; furthermore, there are faculties that are indeterminate yet have wholesome causes and unwholesome objects.
What are the faculties that have unwholesome objects and indeterminate causes?

Answer: There are faculties that are indeterminate (*avyākṛta*) and have unwholesome (*akuśala*) objects. Furthermore, there are faculties that are unwholesome, caused by the indeterminate, and have unwholesome objects. [End of section on unwholesome objects.
Now, regarding those faculties that are caused by the indeterminate, do those faculties have indeterminate objects?
Answer:
Some faculties have an indeterminate cause and take an indeterminate object, a wholesome object, an unwholesome object, or have no object.
What is a faculty that has an indeterminate cause and takes an indeterminate object?

Answer: There are faculties that are indeterminate (avyākṛta) and have indeterminate objects. Furthermore, there are faculties that are unwholesome (akuśala), have indeterminate causes, and have indeterminate objects.
What are the faculties that have indeterminate causes and wholesome (kuśala) objects?

Answer: There are faculties that are indeterminate (*avyākṛta*) while having wholesome (*kuśala*) objects; furthermore, there are faculties that are unwholesome (*akuśala*) while having indeterminate causes and wholesome objects.
What are the faculties that have indeterminate causes and unwholesome objects?

Answer: There are faculties that are indeterminate (*avyākṛta*) while having unwholesome (*akuśala*) objects. Furthermore, there are faculties that are unwholesome, caused by the indeterminate, and having unwholesome objects.
What are the faculties that are caused by the indeterminate and have no objects?
Answer: The faculties have no conditions that are indeterminate dharmas.
Even if the faculties were to have indeterminate dharmas as their conditions:
Are those faculties (indriya) caused by the indeterminate (avyākṛta)? Answer:
Some faculties have the indeterminate as their object (ālambana), are caused by the indeterminate, are caused by the wholesome (kuśala), or are caused by the unwholesome (akuśala).
What are the faculties that have neutral objects and are caused by the neutral?
The answer is:
all neutral faculties that have neutral objects; furthermore, all unwholesome faculties that are caused by the neutral and have neutral objects.
What are the faculties that have the indeterminate as their object and are caused by the wholesome?
The answer is:

those faculties that are wholesome and have the indeterminate as their object; furthermore, those faculties that are indeterminate and are caused by the wholesome while having the indeterminate as their object.
What are the faculties that have indeterminate objects and are caused by the unwholesome? Answer:

Those faculties that are unwholesome and have indeterminate objects; furthermore, those faculties that are indeterminate and are caused by the unwholesome while having indeterminate objects. [End of sections two and three.]
If the various faculties have their causes bound to the desire realm, do those faculties take as their objects that which is bound to the desire realm? Answer:

Some faculties that have their causes bound to the desire realm take as their objects that which is bound to the desire realm, that which is bound to the form realm, that which is bound to the formless realm, that which is unbound, or they have no object at all.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the desire realm and take the desire realm as their object?
Answer: Those faculties that are bound to the desire realm and take the desire realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the desire realm and take the form realm as their object?
Answer: Those faculties that are bound to the desire realm and take the form realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the desire realm and take the form realm as their object? Answer:
Those faculties that are bound to the desire realm and take the form realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the desire realm and take as their object that which is not bound?
Answer: Those faculties that are bound to the desire realm and take as their object that which is not bound.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the desire realm and are without an object? Answer:
Those faculties that are without an object and have as their cause factors bound to the desire realm.
If the various faculties have objects belonging to the desire realm, do those faculties have causes belonging to the desire realm? Answer:

Some faculties that have objects belonging to the desire realm have causes belonging to the desire realm, causes belonging to the form realm, causes belonging to the formless realm, or causes that are unconditioned (unbound).
What are the faculties that have the desire realm as their object and are caused by the desire realm?
Answer: Those faculties that belong to the desire realm and have the desire realm as their object.
What are the faculties that, being bound to the form realm (rūpadhātu), have as their object (ālambana) what is bound to the desire realm (kāmadhātu)?
Answer: Those faculties bound to the form realm that have as their object what is bound to the desire realm.
What are the faculties that are bound to the formless realm (ārūpyadhātu) by way of being conditioned by those bound to the desire realm (kāmadhātu)?
Answer: Those faculties that are bound to the formless realm and have as their object those bound to the desire realm.
What are the faculties that have the desire realm as their object and are not bound by causes? Answer:
All faculties that are not bound and have the desire realm as their object. [End of section on the desire realm.]
If the faculties have their cause in what is bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), do those faculties take as their object (*ālambana*) what is bound to the form realm? Answer:

Some faculties that have their cause in what is bound to the form realm take as their object what is bound to the form realm; some take as their object what is bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*); some take as their object what is bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*); some take as their object what is unbound (*apratisaṃyukta*); and some have no object.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the realm of form and take the realm of form as their object?
Answer: Those faculties that are bound to the realm of form and take the realm of form as their object.
What are the faculties that have their cause bound to the form realm (rūpadhātu) and take as their object that which is bound to the desire realm (kāmadhātu)?
Answer: Those faculties that are bound to the form realm and take as their object that which is bound to the desire realm.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the realm of form (rūpadhātu) and take as their object the realm of formlessness (ārūpyadhātu)? Answer:
Those faculties that are bound to the realm of form and take as their object the realm of formlessness.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the realm of form (rūpadhātu) and take as their object that which is not bound (anāpta)? Answer:
Those faculties that are bound to the realm of form and take as their object that which is not bound.
What are the faculties that are non-objective (anālambana) and have their cause bound to the form realm (rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta)? Answer:
Those faculties that are non-objective and have as their cause factors bound to the form realm.
If various faculties have objects that are bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), do those faculties have causes that are bound to the form realm?

Answer: Some faculties that have objects bound to the form realm have causes that are bound to the form realm; some have causes that are bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*); some have causes that are bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*); and some have causes that are unbound (*apratisaṃyukta*).
What are the faculties that have the form realm as their object and are caused by the form realm? Answer:
All faculties that belong to the form realm and have the form realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have the form realm as their object and are caused by the desire realm?
Answer: Those faculties that belong to the desire realm and have the form realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have the form realm as their object and are caused by the formless realm? Answer:
Those faculties that belong to the formless realm and have the form realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have the color-sphere (rūpadhātu) as their object and are not bound [to any sphere] by way of cause? Answer:
All faculties that are not bound have the color-sphere as their object. [End of section on the color-sphere.]

If the various faculties have their cause (*hetu*) bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), do those faculties have as their object (*ālambana*) that which is bound to the formless realm? Answer:

Some faculties that have their cause bound to the formless realm have as their object that which is bound to the formless realm; some have as their object that which is bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*); some have as their object that which is bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*); some have as their object that which is unbound (*apratisaṃyukta*); and some have no object at all.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the formless realm and take the formless realm as their object? Answer:
Those faculties that are bound to the formless realm and take the formless realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the formless realm and take the desire realm as their object? Answer:
Those faculties that are bound to the formless realm and take the desire realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the formless realm and take the form realm as their object? Answer:
All faculties that are bound to the formless realm and take the form realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have their cause in the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*) and have as their object that which is not bound [to any realm] (*apratisaṃyukta*)? Answer:
Those faculties that are bound to the formless realm and have as their object that which is not bound.
What are the faculties that have no object (anālambana) and are caused by factors bound to the formless realm? Answer:
Those faculties that have no object and are caused by factors bound to the formless realm.

If the various faculties have as their object that which is bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), do those faculties have as their cause that which is bound to the formless realm?

Answer: Some faculties that have as their object that which is bound to the formless realm have as their cause that which is bound to the formless realm; some have as their cause that which is bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*); some have as their cause that which is bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu*); and some have as their cause that which is unbound (*apratisaṃyukta*).
What are the faculties that have the formless realm as their object and are caused by the formless realm?
Answer: All faculties that have the formless realm as their object and are bound to the formless realm.
What are the faculties that have the form realm as their object and are caused by the desire realm?
Answer: Those faculties that belong to the desire realm and have the formless realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have the form realm as their cause and the formless realm as their object? Answer:
Those faculties that belong to the form realm and have the formless realm as their object.
What are the faculties that have the form realm as their object and are not bound by causes? Answer:
All faculties that are not bound have the form realm as their object. (The three triads are concluded.)
If the faculties have learning (*śaikṣa*) as their cause, do those faculties take learning as their object (*ālambana*)? Answer:

Some faculties that have learning as their cause take learning as their object, some take the beyond-learning (*aśaikṣa*) as their object, and some take that which is neither learning nor beyond-learning as their object.
What are the faculties that have training as their cause and are conditioned by training? Answer:
Those faculties that are of training and are conditioned by training; furthermore, those faculties that are beyond training (aśaikṣa) and have training as their cause and are conditioned by training.
What are the faculties that have learning as their cause and the state beyond learning as their condition?
The answer is:

those faculties that are of the nature of learning and have the state beyond learning as their condition; furthermore, those faculties that are of the nature beyond learning and have learning as their cause and the state beyond learning as their condition.
What are the faculties that have training as their cause and are conditioned by that which is neither-training-nor-non-training? Answer:

Those faculties that are of training and are conditioned by that which is neither-training-nor-non-training; furthermore, those faculties that are of non-training and have training as their cause and are conditioned by that which is neither-training-nor-non-training.
If the various faculties have the state of training (śaikṣa) as their object, do those faculties have the state of training as their cause? Answer:

Some faculties that have the state of training as their object have the state of training as their cause, some have the state beyond training (aśaikṣa) as their cause, and some have neither the state of training nor the state beyond training as their cause.
What are the faculties that have the state of training (*śaikṣa*) as their object and have the state of training as their cause?
The answer is:

those faculties that are of the state of training and have the state of training as their object; furthermore, those faculties that are beyond training (*aśaikṣa*) and have the state of training as their cause and the state of training as their object.
What are the faculties that have the state of training (*śaikṣa*) as their object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) and the state beyond training (*aśaikṣa*) as their cause (*hetu*)? Answer:
Those faculties that are beyond training and have the state of training as their object-condition.
What are the faculties that have the "neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee" as their cause and the "trainee" as their object?
Answer: All faculties that are neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee which have the trainee as their object; this concludes the section on the trainee.
If the various faculties have the state beyond training (*aśaikṣa*) as their cause, do those faculties take the state beyond training as their object? Answer:

Some faculties that have the state beyond training as their cause take the state beyond training as their object, some take the state of training (*śaikṣa*) as their object, and some take that which is neither training nor beyond training (*naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣa*) as their object.
What are the faculties that have the aśaikṣa as their cause and the aśaikṣa as their object?
Answer: All faculties that are aśaikṣa and have the aśaikṣa as their object.
What are the faculties that have the aśaikṣa as their cause and the śaikṣa as their object?
Answer: All faculties that are aśaikṣa and have the śaikṣa as their object.
What are the faculties that have the aśaikṣa as their cause and the neither-śaikṣa-nor-aśaikṣa as their condition?
Answer: Those faculties that are aśaikṣa and have the neither-śaikṣa-nor-aśaikṣa as their condition.
If various faculties have the state beyond training (*aśaikṣa*) as their object, do those faculties have the state beyond training as their cause?

Answer: Some faculties that have the state beyond training as their object have the state beyond training as their cause; some have the state of training (*śaikṣa*) as their cause; and some have neither-training-nor-beyond-training as their cause.
What are the faculties that have the unlearned as their object and the unlearned as their cause?
Answer: Those faculties that are unlearned and have the unlearned as their object.
What are the faculties that have the untrained (*aśaikṣa*) as their object and the trained (*śaikṣa*) as their cause? Answer:
Those faculties that are trained and have the untrained as their object; furthermore, those faculties that are untrained and have the trained as their cause and the untrained as their object.
What are the faculties that have the untrained (*aśaikṣa*) as their object and are neither-trained-nor-untrained (*naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣa*) by way of cause? Answer:
All faculties that are neither-trained-nor-untrained which have the untrained as their object. [End of section on the untrained.]
If the various faculties have as their cause that which is neither-learner-nor-non-learner, do those faculties take as their object that which is neither-learner-nor-non-learner?

Answer: Some faculties that have as their cause that which is neither-learner-nor-non-learner take as their object that which is neither-learner-nor-non-learner; some take as their object that which is learner; some take as their object that which is non-learner; and some have no object.
What are the faculties that have a cause which is neither-learner-nor-non-learner and a condition that is neither-learner-nor-non-learner?
Answer: All faculties that are neither-learner-nor-non-learner and have as their condition that which is neither-learner-nor-non-learner.
What are the faculties that have non-learner-and-non-non-learner causes and learner conditions?
Answer: Those faculties that are non-learner-and-non-non-learner and have learner conditions.
What are the faculties that have non-learner-and-non-non-learner causes and learner conditions?
Answer: Those faculties that are non-learner-and-non-non-learner and have learner conditions.
What are the faculties that have as their cause factors that are neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee and are without an object? Answer:
Those faculties that are without an object and have as their cause factors that are neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee.
If the various faculties have non-learner and non-non-learner as their object, do those faculties have non-learner and non-non-learner as their cause?

Answer: Some faculties that have non-learner and non-non-learner as their object have non-learner and non-non-learner as their cause; some have learner as their cause; and some have non-learner as their cause.
What are the faculties that have as their object that which is neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee, and for which the cause is that which is neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee? Answer:
All faculties that are neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee and have as their object that which is neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee.
What are the faculties that have as their object (ālambana) that which is neither-learner-nor-non-learner (naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣa), while having as their cause (hetu) the learner (śaikṣa)? Answer:

Those faculties that are learner (śaikṣa) and have as their object that which is neither-learner-nor-non-learner; furthermore, those faculties that are non-learner (aśaikṣa) and have as their cause the learner, while having as their object that which is neither-learner-nor-non-learner.
What are the faculties that have non-learner (aśaikṣa) as their cause and have neither-learner-nor-non-learner (naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣa) as their object? Answer:
All faculties that are non-learner and have as their object those things that are neither-learner-nor-non-learner. (End of Section 4.3.)
If the faculties have their cause in what is abandoned by seeing the truths (*dṛṣṭi-heya*), do those faculties have as their object (*ālambana*) what is abandoned by seeing the truths? Answer:

Some faculties that have their cause in what is abandoned by seeing the truths have as their object what is abandoned by seeing the truths, some have as their object what is abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), some have as their object what is not abandoned (*aheya*), and some have no object.
What are the faculties that have their cause in what is abandoned by seeing the truths (*satyadarśana-prahātavya*) and take as their object what is abandoned by seeing the truths? Answer:
Those faculties that are themselves abandoned by seeing the truths and take as their object what is abandoned by seeing the truths.
What are the faculties that have their cause in what is abandoned by seeing the truths (*dṛṣṭi-heya*) and take as their object what is abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*)? Answer:

Those faculties that are abandoned by seeing the truths and take as their object what is abandoned by cultivation; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned by cultivation and have as their cause what is abandoned by seeing the truths and take as their object what is abandoned by cultivation.
What are the faculties that have their cause in what is abandoned by seeing the truths (dṛṣṭiheya) and take as their object what is not abandoned (aheya)? Answer:
All faculties that are abandoned by seeing the truths and take as their object what is not abandoned.
What are the faculties that have as their cause factors abandoned through seeing the truths (dṛṣṭi-heya) and are themselves without an object (anālambana)? Answer:
Those faculties that are without an object and have as their cause factors abandoned through seeing the truths.

If the various faculties have as their object that which is abandoned by seeing the truths (*satyadarśana-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by seeing the truths? Answer:

Some faculties that have as their object that which is abandoned by seeing the truths have as their cause that which is abandoned by seeing the truths, some have as their cause that which is abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*), and some have as their cause that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

What are the faculties that are abandoned by seeing the truths (dṛṣṭiheya), have as their object what is abandoned by seeing the truths, and have as their cause what is abandoned by seeing the truths?
Answer: All faculties that are abandoned by seeing the truths, which have as their object what is abandoned by seeing the truths.
What are the faculties that have the truths as their object (*ālambana*), are abandoned by insight (*darśana-prahātavya*), and have thought-cultivation as their cause (*hetu*)?
The answer is:
those faculties that are abandoned by thought-cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*) and have the truths as their object.
What are the faculties that have as their object [states] abandoned by seeing the truths (dṛṣṭi-heya), while having as their cause [states] not abandoned? Answer:
All faculties that are not abandoned and have as their object [states] abandoned by seeing the truths; this concludes the section on those abandoned by seeing the truths.
If the faculties have thought-abandonment (*bhāvanā-heya*) as their cause, do those faculties have thought-abandonment as their object?

Answer: Some faculties that have thought-abandonment as their cause have thought-abandonment as their object; some have vision-of-truth-abandonment (*darśana-heya*) as their object; some have non-abandonment as their object; and some have no object.
What are the faculties that have thought-abandonment as their cause and thought-abandonment as their object?
Answer: Those faculties that are themselves thought-abandonment and have thought-abandonment as their object.
What are the faculties that have cultivation-abandonment as their cause and have truth-seeing-abandonment as their object?
Answer: Those faculties that have cultivation-abandonment as their cause and have truth-seeing-abandonment as their object.
What are the faculties that have thought-elimination (*cintāmayaprahāṇa*) as their cause and non-elimination (*aprahāṇa*) as their object? Answer:
All faculties that have thought-elimination as their cause and non-elimination as their object.
What are the faculties that have their cause in [factors] to be abandoned by cultivation and are without an object? Answer:
Those faculties that are without an object and have as their cause factors to be abandoned by cultivation.
If the various faculties have thought-abandonment (*cintāmayaprahāṇa*) as their object-condition, do those faculties have thought-abandonment as their cause-condition?

Answer: Some faculties that have thought-abandonment as their object-condition have thought-abandonment as their cause-condition; some have the abandonment through seeing the truths (*darśanaprahāṇa*) as their cause-condition; and some have no [abandonment] as their cause-condition.
What are the faculties that have thought-elimination as their condition and have thought-elimination as their cause?
Answer: All faculties that have thought-elimination as their condition and have thought-elimination as their cause.
What are the faculties that have thought-elimination (bhāvanā-heya) as their object-condition and have vision-of-truth-elimination (darśana-heya) as their cause? Answer:

Those faculties that are vision-of-truth-elimination and have thought-elimination as their object-condition; furthermore, those faculties that are thought-elimination and have vision-of-truth-elimination as their cause and thought-elimination as their object-condition.
What are the faculties that have thought-elimination as their object and are caused by what is not to be eliminated? Answer:
All faculties that are not to be eliminated and have thought-elimination as their object. [End of section on thought-elimination.]
If the various faculties have non-abandonment (*aprahāṇa*) as their cause, do those faculties have non-abandonment as their object (*ālambana*)? Answer:

Some faculties have non-abandonment as their cause and have non-abandonment as their object; some have non-abandonment as their cause and have what is abandoned by seeing the truths (*darśana-prahātavya*) as their object; and some have non-abandonment as their cause and have what is abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*) as their object.
What are the faculties that have non-interruption as their cause and non-interruption as their condition?
The answer is:
those faculties that have non-interruption as their condition.
What are the faculties that have non-abandonment as their cause and are abandoned by insight into the truths?
Answer: All faculties that have non-abandonment as their cause and are abandoned by insight into the truths.
What are the faculties that have non-abandonment as their cause and are conditioned by what is to be abandoned through cultivation?
Answer: All faculties that have non-abandonment as their cause and are conditioned by what is to be abandoned through cultivation.
If the various faculties have non-abandonment (*aprahāṇa*) as their object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), do those faculties have non-abandonment as their cause-condition (*hetu-pratyaya*)? Answer:

Some faculties that have non-abandonment as their object-condition have non-abandonment as their cause-condition; some have the abandonment through seeing the truths (*darśana-heya*) as their cause-condition; and some have the abandonment through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) as their cause-condition.
What are the faculties that have non-abandonment as their object and for which non-abandonment is the cause?
Answer: Those faculties that are non-abandoned and have non-abandonment as their object.
What are the faculties that have the uninterrupted as their object and are caused by what is abandoned through seeing the truths?
Answer: Those faculties that are abandoned through seeing the truths and have the uninterrupted as their object.
What are the faculties that have the uninterrupted (*anantarya*) as their object-condition and are abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*)? Answer:
All faculties abandoned by cultivation that have the uninterrupted as their object-condition. (The five and three [categories] are concluded.)

If the faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their object (*ālambana*) that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering?

Answer: Some faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering, and they have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering; some have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya*); some have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha*); some have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*); some have as their object that which is abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā*); some have as their object that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*); and some are without an object (*anālambana*).
What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) and have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering? Answer:

Those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), are caused by what is abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering.

What are the faculties that have their cause in the abandonment through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) and have their object in the abandonment through the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have their object in the abandonment through the vision of origination; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of origination and have their cause in the abandonment through the vision of suffering and have their object in the abandonment through the vision of origination.

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) and have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*)? Answer:
They are those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation.

Furthermore, there are faculties whose cause for abandonment through the vision of the origin is abandoned through the vision of cessation, and whose condition for abandonment through the vision of the origin is abandoned through the vision of cessation; furthermore, there are faculties whose cause for abandonment through the vision of cessation is abandoned through the vision of suffering, and whose condition for abandonment through the vision of cessation is abandoned through the vision of cessation.

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the path; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), are caused by what is abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the path; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of the path, are caused by what is abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the path.

What are the faculties that have their cause in the abandonment through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) and have their object in the abandonment through reflection (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have their object in the abandonment through reflection; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), have their cause in the abandonment through the vision of suffering, and have their object in the abandonment through reflection; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through reflection, have their cause in the abandonment through the vision of suffering, and have their object in the abandonment through reflection.

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their cause [other factors] abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object those not to be abandoned (*aprahātavyālambana*)? Answer:

Those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) and the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), and which have as their cause [factors] abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object those not to be abandoned.
What are the faculties that have as their cause the abandonment through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya) and are without objects? Answer:
Those faculties that are without objects and have as their cause dharmas to be abandoned through the vision of suffering.

If the various faculties have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering?

Answer: Some faculties that have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering have as their cause that which is abandoned by the vision of suffering; some have as their cause that which is abandoned by the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*); some have as their cause that which is abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*); and some have as their cause that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

What are the faculties that, having the cessation of suffering as their object (*ālambana*), are abandoned through the vision of the cessation of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), and have the cessation of suffering as their cause (*hetu*)?
The answer is:

those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of the cessation of suffering and have the cessation of suffering as their object; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of the origin of suffering (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), have the cessation of suffering as their cause, and have the cessation of suffering as their object.

What are the faculties that have seeing suffering as their object (*ālambana*), are abandoned through seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), and have seeing origination as their cause (*hetu*)?
The answer is:

those faculties that are abandoned through seeing origination and have seeing suffering as their object; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned through seeing suffering, have seeing origination as their cause, and have seeing suffering as their object.
What are the faculties that have seeing the suffering (duḥkha-darśana) as their object-condition and are abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanā-heya)? Answer:
Those faculties that are abandoned by cultivation and have seeing the suffering as their object-condition.

What are the faculties that have as their object [dharmas] abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), while having as their cause those that are not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*)? Answer:
All faculties that are not to be abandoned which take as their object [dharmas] abandoned through the vision of suffering; this concludes the Truth of Suffering.
The causes for the abandonment through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) and the conditions for the abandonment through the vision of the origin are also as stated above.

Regarding those faculties whose causes are abandoned through the vision of the cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), are those faculties also conditioned by what is abandoned through the vision of the cessation?
The answer is: Yes.

Some faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned through the vision of the cessation [of suffering] (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), and they take as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the cessation, that which is not to be abandoned, or that which is without an object.
How is it that a faculty has as its cause that which is abandoned through the vision of the cessation and takes as its object that which is abandoned through the vision of the cessation?
Answer: The faculties that are abandoned through the vision of the cessation [of suffering] take as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the cessation.
How is it that a faculty has its cause in that which is abandoned through the vision of the cessation, yet takes as its object that which is not abandoned?
Answer: The faculties that are abandoned through the vision of cessation take as their object that which is not abandoned.
How is it that a faculty has the vision of cessation as its cause but does not have [that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation] as its object?
Answer: Are there faculties that do not have as their object (ālambana) dharmas abandoned through the vision of cessation (nirodhadarśana-prahātavya)?

Furthermore, if faculties have as their object dharmas abandoned through the vision of cessation, do those faculties themselves have as their cause (hetu) dharmas abandoned through the vision of cessation?
Answer:

Some faculties have as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya), and are caused by that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation, caused by that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya), caused by that which is abandoned through the vision of origin (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya), caused by that which is abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-prahātavya), or caused by that which is not to be abandoned (aprahātavya).
What are the faculties that, having as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation, have as their cause that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation?
The answer is:
those faculties that are abandoned by the vision of cessation and have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation.

What are the faculties that have cessation as their object (*ālambana*), are abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), and have suffering as their cause (*hetu*) while being abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties that are abandoned by the vision of suffering and have cessation as their object; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned by the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), are abandoned by the vision of suffering, and have cessation as their object; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned by the vision of cessation, are abandoned by the vision of suffering, and have cessation as their object.

What are the faculties that, having the cessation of suffering as their object (*ālambana*), are abandoned through the vision of the cessation of suffering (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), yet have as their cause (*hetu*) those things abandoned through the vision of the origin of suffering (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties abandoned through the vision of the origin of suffering which take as their object those things abandoned through the vision of the cessation of suffering; furthermore, those faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering which have as their cause those things abandoned through the vision of the origin of suffering and take as their object those things abandoned through the vision of the cessation of suffering; furthermore, those faculties abandoned through the vision of the cessation of suffering which have as their cause those things abandoned through the vision of the origin of suffering and take as their object those things abandoned through the vision of the cessation of suffering.
What are the faculties that have as their object those things abandoned by the vision of the cessation [of suffering], while having as their cause those things abandoned by cultivation?
Answer: Those faculties abandoned by cultivation which have as their object those things abandoned by the vision of the cessation [of suffering].
What are the faculties that have cessation through seeing (*darśana-heya*) as their object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), while having non-abandonment (*aheya*) as their cause? Answer:
All faculties that are non-abandoned and have cessation through seeing as their object-condition, up to the truth of cessation (*nirodha-satya*).
Having finished the four truths as above regarding those [factors] abandoned by seeing the path which take what is abandoned by seeing the path as their object:

If various faculties have their causes abandoned by seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), do those faculties have their objects abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna*)?

Answer: Some faculties have as their cause that which is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), while they are conditioned by (*ālambana*) that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*), or abandoned through the subsequent knowledge regarding suffering (*duḥkha-anvayajñāna-prahātavya*); or conditioned by that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding origin (*samudaya-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*), or abandoned through the subsequent knowledge regarding origin (*samudaya-anvayajñāna-prahātavya*); or conditioned by that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*), or abandoned through the subsequent knowledge regarding cessation (*nirodha-anvayajñāna-prahātavya*); or conditioned by that which is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path (*mārga-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*), or abandoned through the subsequent knowledge regarding the path (*mārga-anvayajñāna-prahātavya*); or conditioned by that which is abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*); or conditioned by that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*); or they have no object-condition (*anālambana*).

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have suffering as their object (*ālambana*), and are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkhe dharmajñāna*)? Answer:

Those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have suffering as their object, and furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), have the vision of suffering as their cause (*hetu*), and have suffering as their object.

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have suffering as their object (*ālambana*), and are abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna*)? Answer:

Those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have suffering as their object, and furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), have the vision of suffering as their cause (*hetu*), and have suffering as their object.

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their object the factors abandoned through the knowledge of the origin (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object the factors abandoned through the knowledge of the origin; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of the origin and have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and as their object the factors abandoned through the knowledge of the origin.

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their object the path of the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*), and are themselves abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination? Answer:

Those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object the subsequent knowledge of origination; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of origination, which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object the subsequent knowledge of origination.

What are the faculties (*indriya*) that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*), and are themselves abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation? Answer:

They are the various faculties abandoned through the vision of suffering that have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation; furthermore, those various faculties abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation; furthermore, those various faculties abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) which have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation.

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their object the knowledge of the unknown regarding cessation (*nirodha-ajñāna-aparijñāna-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object the knowledge of the unknown regarding cessation; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object the knowledge of the unknown regarding cessation; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object the knowledge of the unknown regarding cessation.

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path (*mārga-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), are caused by [faculties] abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), are caused by [faculties] abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object the knowledge of the dharma regarding the path.
What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their object the path not-yet-known wisdom (*mārga-ajñāna-jñāna-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of suffering and have as their object the path not-yet-known wisdom; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object the path not-yet-known wisdom; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the vision of origin, have as their cause those abandoned through the vision of suffering, and have as their object the path not-yet-known wisdom.
What are the faculties that have suffering as their object of vision for abandonment (*duḥkha-darśana-heya*) and are conditioned by abandonment through reflection (*bhāvanā-heya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties that have suffering as their object of vision for abandonment and are conditioned by abandonment through reflection; furthermore, those faculties that have the origin [of suffering] as their object of vision for abandonment and have suffering as their cause for abandonment and are conditioned by abandonment through reflection.

Furthermore, regarding those faculties that have their cause in what is abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) and whose object is what is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-heya*):
how is it that a faculty has its cause in what is abandoned through the vision of suffering and its object in what is not to be abandoned (*aheya*)?

Regarding those faculties that have as their cause what is abandoned by the vision of exhaustion (*kṣayajñāna*) and the vision of the path (*mārgajñāna*), and have as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkhadarśana*) but are themselves not abandoned:
how are there faculties that have as their cause what is abandoned by the vision of suffering but have no object? Answer:
Regarding those faculties that have no object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) and are abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*):
if those faculties have as their object something abandoned by the vision of suffering, are those faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*)?
Answer: No.

Alternatively, there are faculties that take as their object what is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), yet have as their cause what is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*), what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge regarding suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*), what is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*), what is abandoned through the subsequent knowledge regarding origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*), what is abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*), or what is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

What are the faculties that have as their object (*ālambana*) what is abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), while having as their cause (*hetu*) what is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties which have as their cause what is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering and have as their object what is abandoned through the vision of suffering; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna-prahātavya*), have as their cause what is abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering, and have as their object what is abandoned through the vision of suffering.

Those faculties that are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and have as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (samudaye ’nvaya-jñāna-prahātavya), which have as their cause what is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering and have as their object what is abandoned by the vision of suffering.
What are the faculties that have the cessation through seeing suffering as their object and are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination?
Answer: Those faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination which have the cessation through seeing suffering as their object.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghadeva of Kaśmīra and Zhu Fonian during the Fu Qin dynasty, from the *Mūlavastu* (Root Chapter), the second part of the *Saptapratyayavarga* (Section on the Seven Conditions): Furthermore, when the various faculties (*indriya*) are abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*), they have as their cause those [faculties] abandoned through the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination (*samudaya-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*), and as their condition those [factors] abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkhadarśana-prahātavya*).

What are the faculties that have suffering as their object (*ālambana*), are abandoned by the knowledge of the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga*) regarding suffering, and have the subsequent knowledge of the path of cultivation (*bhāvanā-mārga*) regarding origin as their cause?

those faculties that are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of the path of cultivation regarding origin and have suffering as their object while being abandoned by the knowledge of the path of seeing regarding suffering; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of the path of seeing regarding suffering and have the subsequent knowledge of the path of cultivation regarding origin as their cause while having suffering as their object.

those faculties that are abandoned by cultivation and have seeing the suffering as their condition.

Regarding those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of the truth of cessation (*nirodha-satya*): are those faculties abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna*)?
Answer:

What are the faculties that have their cause in the abandonment through seeing (*darśana-prahāṇa*) and have as their object the factors abandoned through the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣaya-jñāna*)? Answer:
Those faculties that are abandoned through seeing and have as their object the factors abandoned through the knowledge of exhaustion.

What are the faculties that are abandoned through the vision of the destruction [of the outflows], yet have as their object that which is to be abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of the destruction?
Answer: Those faculties that are abandoned through the vision of the destruction and have as their object that which is to be abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of the destruction.
What are the faculties that have their cause in what is abandoned by the vision of cessation, yet take as their object what is not abandoned?
Answer: Those faculties that are abandoned by the vision of cessation and take as their object what is not abandoned.
What are the faculties that have as their cause the abandonment through seeing (darśana-heya), yet are without an object (anālambana)? Answer:
Those faculties that are without an object and have as their cause dharmas to be abandoned through seeing.

If the various faculties (*indriya*) have as their object (*ālambana*) that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), do those faculties have as their cause (*hetu*) that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation (*nirodha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*)?

Answer: Some faculties have as their object that which is abandoned by the vision of cessation, while having as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of cessation; some have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvayajñāna-prahātavya*); some have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of suffering (*duḥkha-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*); some have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvayajñāna-prahātavya*); some have as their cause that which is abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma of origination (*samudaya-dharmajñāna-prahātavya*); some have as their cause that which is abandoned by the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvayajñāna-prahātavya*); some have as their cause that which is abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*); and some have as their cause that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).
What are the faculties that, having the cessation-seeing as their condition, have the cessation-dharma-knowledge-abandonment as their cause?
Answer: Those faculties that are cessation-dharma-knowledge-abandonment and have the cessation-seeing as their condition.

Those faculties that are abandoned through the knowledge of the unknown have the cessation through seeing as their object-condition.

What are the faculties that, having the cessation of suffering as their object (*ālambana*), are abandoned by the vision of cessation (*darśana-prahātavya*), while having the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering (*duḥkha-dharma-jñāna*) as their cause (*hetu*) for abandonment?

those faculties which are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering and have the cessation of suffering as their object; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding origination (*samudaya-dharma-jñāna*) and have the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering as their cause for abandonment, while having the cessation of suffering as their object; furthermore, those faculties which are abandoned by the knowledge of the dharma regarding cessation (*nirodha-dharma-jñāna*) and have the knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering as their cause for abandonment, while having the cessation of suffering as their object.

What are the faculties that have as their object the abandonment through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), while having as their cause the abandonment through the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna-prahātavya*)?
The answer is:

those faculties that are abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of suffering and have as their object the abandonment through the vision of cessation; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) and have as their cause the abandonment through the subsequent knowledge of suffering and as their object the abandonment through the vision of cessation; furthermore, those faculties that are abandoned through the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) and have as their cause the abandonment through the subsequent knowledge of suffering and as their object the abandonment through the vision of cessation.
